word: CompTIA troubleshooting process: Preventive measures, implementing
definition: proactive steps taken to stop the identified issue from occurring again such as updating firmware changing settings or educating users
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The same technical issue occurs repeatedly on the same device or across multiple workstations.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Based on the root cause, apply 'Group Policy' updates, schedule regular maintenance (like 'disk cleanup'), install software patches, or provide training to prevent human-caused errors.

word: CompTIA troubleshooting process: Probable cause, theories of
definition: the process of creating a logical hypothesis for why a failure has occurred based on observed evidence and technical knowledge
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Misdiagnosis of hardware vs. software issues, resulting in unnecessary component replacement.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Question the user, check system logs (such as the 'Event Viewer' in Windows), and perform visual inspections to narrow down the list of possibilities, starting with the simplest cause (the OSI (Open Systems Interconnection) model approach).

definition: any hardware software or networking inconsistency that prevents a device or service from performing its intended function
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Error codes, system hangs, BSOD (Blue Screen of Death), or complete failure of components to initialize.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Apply the CompTIA seven-step methodology: gather information, replicate the problem, perform diagnostics, apply a fix, verify results, and document.

definition: a windows administrative tool that consolidates several management consoles including 'disk management' 'device manager' and 'event viewer' into a single utility
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Inability to manage storage volumes, update drivers, or view system logs, leading to maintenance difficulties.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Right-click the 'Start' button and select 'Computer Management' or press 'Win + R', type 'compmgmt.msc', and press 'Enter'.

word: Computer Name/Domain Changes dialog box, Windows 10
definition: a legacy system configuration window used to rename a computer or join it to a workgroup or a windows domain a network environment managed by a domain controller
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Inability to join a network domain, access shared network resources, or resolve network identification errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the 'System' properties (or 'About' settings), click 'Advanced system settings', go to the 'Computer Name' tab, and click the 'Change' button to update the hostname or domain membership.

definition: the various graphical interfaces including the 'settings' app and control panel used to modify system behaviors user preferences and hardware settings
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Incorrect system time, display issues, or failed network connections due to misconfiguration.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the 'Settings' app or search the Start menu for the specific control applet, or run the command 'control' to access the classic Control Panel for advanced settings.

definition: the process of setting up short-range wireless communication between a computer and a peripheral device like a mouse or headset
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Device pairing failure, inability to discover new hardware, or intermittent connection drops.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the Bluetooth radio is enabled, put the peripheral into 'pairing mode', and go to 'Settings > Devices > Bluetooth & other devices' to add the new device.

definition: adjusting web browser settings for privacy security such as certificate management and performance like caching or proxy usage
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Web pages failing to load, security warning prompts, or slow performance while surfing the internet.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the browser’s settings menu, clear the 'cached images and files', check 'privacy and security' settings, or reset the browser to default configurations if issues persist.

definition: setting up a workstation to recognize and authenticate against a central directory service typically active directory in a windows network
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Trust relationship' errors, login failures, or inability to access network resources (like file servers).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify network connectivity to the domain controller, ensure the computer’s DNS (Domain Name System) settings point to the domain server, and re-join the domain via the 'Computer Name/Domain Changes' dialog.

definition: setting up an email client like microsoft outlook to connect to mail servers using protocols such as imap internet message access protocol or pop3 post office protocol version 3 and smtp simple mail transfer protocol
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unable to connect to server', 'Authentication failure', or emails stuck in the Outbox.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the server addresses, port numbers (e.g., '993' for IMAP, '465' or '587' for SMTP), and ensure the username and password credentials are correct.

definition: establishing rules on a soho small office home office router to block or permit incoming and outgoing traffic based on port numbers ip addresses or protocols
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Inability to access certain websites, blocked gaming services, or vulnerabilities due to open ports.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Access the router’s web interface, navigate to the 'Firewall' or 'Port Forwarding' section, and define rules to block or allow specific traffic as needed.

definition: assigning settings such as ip address subnet mask and default gateway to a network interface using the ipv4 internet protocol version 4 standard
ERROR SYMPTOMS: IP address conflict' errors, no network access, or inability to communicate outside the local subnet.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Access 'Network Connections' in the Control Panel, right-click the adapter, select 'Properties', choose 'Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4)', and configure either a static IP or 'Obtain an IP address automatically' (DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol)).

definition: setting up a network interface to support the 128-bit addressing scheme of ipv6 internet protocol version 6 designed to replace ipv4
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Inability to connect to services that require IPv6 or connectivity issues when IPv6 is incorrectly configured in a mixed-protocol environment.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Go to the adapter’s 'Properties', enable 'Internet Protocol Version 6 (TCP/IPv6)', and ensure the address is either set to automatic (via SLAAC (Stateless Address Autoconfiguration)) or manually configured if required.

definition: a utility used to troubleshoot the windows boot process by enabling or disabling startup services drivers and boot options
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Slow boot times, system instability, or problematic software starting automatically at login.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Run 'msconfig', navigate to the 'Services' or 'Startup' tabs, selectively disable non-essential items, and restart the system to test performance.

definition: the process of setting up network parameters ips dns ssids to ensure devices can communicate effectively over a lan local area network or wan wide area network
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Network unreachable', 'DNS server not responding', or inability to access the internet.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check physical connections, verify IP/DNS configurations, run the command 'ipconfig /all' to check settings, and reset the network adapter.

definition: adding printer drivers setting print queues and configuring network settings for printers or mfds multifunction devices that print scan and copy
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Printer offline, documents not printing, or the scanner not being detected by the computer.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use 'Devices and Printers' to add the device, ensure the correct driver is installed, and verify the IP address if using a network-attached printer.

definition: setting up a computer to route its internet traffic through an intermediary proxy server often for security or content filtering
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Internet traffic being blocked, browser 'connection refused' errors, or inability to access internal resources.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Navigate to 'Settings > Network & Internet > Proxy', disable the proxy if not needed, or update the proxy server address and port to match the network requirements.

definition: setting up an ssid encryption type like wpa3 wi-fi protected access 3 and security passwords to connect a device to a wireless access point
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Authentication failed', weak signal, or inability to find the SSID.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the password, ensure the wireless radio is turned on, update the wireless network adapter driver, and confirm compatibility between the client and the access point’s security settings.

definition: a communication process where a reliable connection is established before data is exchanged using a three-way handshake syn syn-ack ack
ERROR SYMPTOMS: High latency or dropped connections during data-heavy transfers, or 'Connection timed out' errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure both the sender and receiver are reachable, check for firewall rules blocking the specific port, and verify that the path between them is not experiencing high packet loss.

definition: a tab in the 'internet options' utility within the windows control panel used for configuring dial-up vpn virtual private network and lan proxy settings
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Issues with VPN connectivity or persistent proxy errors preventing internet access.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open 'Control Panel', search for 'Internet Options', click the 'Connections' tab, and review the LAN settings or the list of configured VPN/dial-up connections.

definition: the process of limiting access to network resources based on user identity or device status often managed via acls access control lists
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Access denied' messages when attempting to open shared folders or network applications.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the permissions on the target resource, verify that the user is in the correct security group, and ensure the account is not locked out or disabled.

definition: a type of dsl technology where data transmission speeds are higher for downloading than for uploading commonly used for residential broadband
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Slow upload speeds, frequent disconnections during data transfers, or complete lack of internet connectivity.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the ADSL filter is correctly installed on the phone line, check the modem/router’s synchronization status lights, and verify the cabling from the wall jack.

definition: wireless personal area network connectivity between devices using the 2 4 ghz frequency band
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Audio stuttering, mouse/keyboard latency, or failure to maintain a connection.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Keep devices within range, move away from sources of interference (like 2.4 GHz cordless phones), and restart the Bluetooth radio.

definition: broadband internet access provided over the same coaxial cabling infrastructure used for cable television
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Internet speed drops during peak hours, connection timeout, or 'No signal' on the modem.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the coaxial cable is securely tightened, check the status lights on the modem, and contact the ISP (Internet Service Provider) to ensure the service is active.

definition: cables that connect the computer case s front-panel features like the power button reset button and hdd hard disk drive activity light to the motherboard
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The computer won't turn on, the power button does nothing, or the LEDs on the case do not light up.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Consult the motherboard manual for the pin-out diagram, ensure every connector is seated on the correct pins, and check for loose or damaged wires.

definition: wireless connectivity for mobile devices utilizing cellular towers e g 4g lte long-term evolution 5g to provide data access
ERROR SYMPTOMS: No signal, 'No SIM card inserted' errors, or extremely slow data speeds.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Toggle 'Airplane Mode' on and off, ensure the SIM card is seated correctly, and verify that cellular data is enabled in the device settings.

definition: a type of copper cable with a central conductor used primarily for cable internet and television signals
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Signal attenuation (loss), intermittent internet, or pixelated cable TV.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Inspect for kinks or damage, ensure F-connectors are tight, and use a multimeter to check for continuity if a break is suspected.

definition: a twisted-pair ethernet cable used to connect similar devices e g computer to computer by swapping the transmit and receive pairs
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Two directly connected devices failing to communicate.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the cable type is correct (many modern NICs (Network Interface Cards) now support Auto-MDIX and can auto-sense the connection type).

definition: a legacy connection method that uses the public switched telephone network to establish an internet connection via a modem
ERROR SYMPTOMS: High-pitched connection noises failing to establish, or extremely slow data transfer speeds.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the telephone line connection, verify the modem is configured correctly in Device Manager, and ensure the ISP phone number is accurate.

definition: a modern digital display interface used to connect video sources like graphics cards to display devices monitors
ERROR SYMPTOMS: No image, flickering, or incorrect resolution.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the cable is plugged in completely, test with a known-good cable, and verify that the monitor’s input source is set to DisplayPort.

definition: a technology that provides high-speed internet access over existing copper telephone lines
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Frequent drops in connection or poor line quality.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check all microfilters in the home to ensure they are on the correct devices (e.g., phones), and verify the DSL modem status lights.

definition: a digital display interface used to connect a video source to a display device commonly seen in older monitors
ERROR SYMPTOMS: No display or distorted colors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check for bent pins on the connector, ensure the screws are tightened, and verify the DVI port type.

definition: the process of diagnosing issues with sending or receiving email involving server connectivity authentication and protocol settings
ERROR SYMPTOMS: SMTP authentication error', 'Server not found', or incoming mail not syncing.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check internet access, verify server settings and port numbers, ensure credentials are valid, and confirm that the antivirus/firewall is not blocking the mail client.

definition: a high-speed transmission medium that uses light pulses traveling through glass or plastic threads to carry data
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Total loss of connectivity or intermittent signal drops.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Inspect connectors for dust or damage, ensure the cable has not been bent past its minimum bend radius, and use a light meter if signal loss is suspected.

definition: a proprietary audio video interface for transmitting uncompressed video data and compressed or uncompressed digital audio data to display devices
ERROR SYMPTOMS: No audio, no video, or 'Out of range' resolution error.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use a different HDMI cable, ensure both the monitor and the PC are set to the correct resolution, and update the graphics drivers.

definition: a legacy standard for connecting storage devices hard drives optical drives to the motherboard
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Drive not detected, or BIOS/UEFI boot errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the IDE cable is oriented correctly (pin 1 alignment), set the master/slave jumpers correctly on the drive, and test with a different cable.

definition: the step-by-step approach to identifying why a device cannot connect to the internet
ERROR SYMPTOMS: No internet access' warning, or DNS errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Run 'ipconfig' to check the default gateway, verify DNS resolution (e.g., 'nslookup google.com'), and test the physical connection or wireless access point.

definition: a proprietary computer bus and power connector developed by apple for mobile devices
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Device not charging, or not being recognized by a computer.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Clean debris from the port, use an Apple-certified cable, and check the power adapter.

definition: a common issue where physical cables or modules are not securely seated causing intermittent performance or failure
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System crashes, peripherals disconnecting, or blinking LED status lights.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Physically check every cable (power, data, video) and peripheral connection, reseating them if they appear loose or unsecured.

definition: software that allows organizations to manage specific apps on mobile devices ensuring corporate data remains secure
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Corporate apps failing to launch or blocking access to sensitive data.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check if the device is still enrolled in the MDM system, and ensure that the app is authorized and updated.

definition: a security software solution that allows it administrators to control secure and enforce policies on mobile devices
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Device not syncing, remote wipe initiated, or inability to access internal resources.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the device has internet access to communicate with the MDM server, and check that the user account is in good standing within the management console.

definition: fiber optic cabling designed to carry multiple light rays modes simultaneously over shorter distances
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data corruption or signal attenuation over long cable runs.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify that the cable length does not exceed the manufacturer’s specification (usually shorter than single-mode), and inspect connectors for cleanliness.

definition: the infrastructure and protocols enabling computers to share resources
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Inability to browse the network, file sharing timeouts.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Confirm the NIC is active, verify IP configuration, and check network switch/router port status.

definition: cabling with a fire-resistant jacket designed for use in plenum spaces areas between floors or ceilings used for air circulation
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Non-compliance with building codes or potential fire hazard if standard (non-plenum) cable is used.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Identify the cable jacket label ('CMP'); if incorrect, replace with plenum-rated cabling for local building code compliance.

definition: a condition where a network interface on a switch repeatedly transitions between 'up' and 'down' states
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Intermittent connectivity, high latency, or network instability.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Inspect physical cables, check for port configuration mismatches (speed/duplex settings), or replace the suspect switch port or cable.

definition: physical cables from the psu power supply unit that provide power to motherboard components storage drives and gpus
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System won't power up, or specific devices (like fans or drives) not receiving power.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure cables are firmly seated; use a multimeter to check for correct voltages.

definition: the process of diagnosing printer connectivity issues whether local or network-attached
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Printer shows 'Offline', job stuck in queue, or device not recognized.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify physical connectivity, power cycle the printer, clear the print spooler, and update drivers.

definition: a reference of standard network ports and protocols used for identifying and troubleshooting service connectivity
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Inability to connect to specific services (like mail or web) due to blocked ports.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Consult the standard port list to verify that the application is using the correct port and that firewalls are allowing traffic for that specific port.

definition: a technology that allows a user to connect to and control a computer in a different location as if they were sitting in front of it
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Connection refused', 'Authentication failed', or lagging interface.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure Remote Desktop is enabled on the target machine, verify network connectivity, and ensure the port is open on the host firewall.

definition: a common type of coaxial cable used for high-bandwidth applications like cable tv and broadband internet
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Signal loss or intermittent internet connectivity.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the connectors are crimped correctly and the center conductor is straight and undamaged.

definition: the standard connector and cable type used for ethernet networking in home and office environments
ERROR SYMPTOMS: No network access or link lights off.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Inspect the plug for broken locking tabs, ensure wires are correctly pinned (T568B standard), and check for damaged copper strands.

definition: a standard interface for connecting storage devices ssds and hdds to the motherboard
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Drive not detected in BIOS or system failing to boot.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Swap the SATA cable, try a different SATA port on the motherboard, and ensure the power connector is also attached to the drive.

definition: internet access provided via a satellite in orbit used in remote areas where cable or dsl are unavailable
ERROR SYMPTOMS: High latency (ping), weather-related signal outages, or slow speeds.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the satellite dish is clear of obstructions, check alignment, and restart the satellite modem.

definition: a type of fiber optic connector known for its push-pull latching mechanism
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Poor signal or failed fiber connection.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Inspect the fiber tip for contaminants and ensure the connector is fully seated into the transceiver.

definition: a legacy set of standards for physically connecting and transferring data between computers and peripheral devices mostly used for high-performance servers
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Device not detected or SCSI bus errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure all devices on the bus have unique IDs and that the bus is properly terminated at both ends.

definition: a dsl technology that provides equal bandwidth for both uploading and downloading data
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Connectivity failure or inconsistent speeds.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the line condition and modem settings, ensuring that the service plan supports symmetric speeds.

definition: protecting the communication channel and the data transmitted through it
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data breaches, unauthorized access, or man-in-the-middle attacks.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Enforce encryption, use secure protocols, and implement strong authentication.

definition: a legacy connection type used for transmitting data one bit at a time over a single channel
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Peripheral (like a barcode scanner or console) not responding.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the COM port settings (baud rate, parity, data bits) in Device Manager match the peripheral requirements.

definition: fiber optic cabling designed to carry a single ray of light mode over very long distances
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Signal attenuation or connectivity failure over long runs.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the cable is not bent, check for connector cleanliness, and verify the transceiver type matches the cable type.

definition: a fiber optic connector that uses a bayonet-style twist-lock mechanism
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Intermittent signal or connection failure.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Clean the fiber tip, ensure the connector is twisted and locked properly into the port.

definition: the standard wiring configuration for ethernet cables where the pin-outs are the same on both ends used to connect dissimilar devices e g switch to computer
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Device not communicating with the network switch.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the cable type is straight-through and not crossover, and check for damaged wiring pairs.

definition: an older analog video standard that provides higher resolution than standard vga
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Low resolution, blurry images, or incorrect color representation.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the cable is secure, test with a different monitor, and verify that the graphics card driver supports the high-resolution modes.

definition: the process of keeping data consistent between devices e g smartphone and cloud
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Files out-of-sync, outdated information, or synchronization conflicts.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check internet connectivity, verify account credentials, and restart the synchronization client.

definition: an endpoint for communication between two devices defined by an ip address and a port number
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Connection refused' or failure to establish a service connection.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the 'netstat' command to check the status of socket connections and ensure the target service is listening on the expected port.

definition: a high-speed interface that supports both data and video displayport using the usb-c connector
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Thunderbolt device not detected or slow transfer speeds.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the cable is a 'Thunderbolt-certified' cable, update the Thunderbolt controller drivers, and verify the device is plugged into a Thunderbolt-enabled port.

definition: general diagnostic activities for resolving any connectivity-related failure
ERROR SYMPTOMS: General loss of connectivity, intermittent signals, or system errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check physical connections, verify network settings, test with different hardware, and use CLI tools like 'ping' or 'tracert'.

definition: a type of cable where pairs of insulated copper wires are twisted together to reduce electromagnetic interference
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Slow speeds or network interference.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Keep cables away from fluorescent lights or motors, check for damage, and verify that the cable category meets the network speed requirements.

definition: the most common interface for connecting peripherals to a computer
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Device not recognized, or slow transfer speeds.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Try a different port, update the USB controller drivers in Device Manager, and test the peripheral on another system.

definition: a device that allows a system to connect to a wired network using a usb port instead of a built-in ethernet port
ERROR SYMPTOMS: No network connection or driver errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify that the adapter is correctly seated, install the manufacturer’s driver, and check that the device is detected in Device Manager.

definition: the most common type of networking cable consisting of twisted pairs without shielding against emi
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Cross-talk or slow data transmission.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure cable runs do not exceed the 100-meter limit and keep cables away from major sources of interference.

definition: a legacy analog video interface used for monitors and projectors
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Poor image quality, no image, or 'ghosting' effects.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Inspect the 15-pin connector for bent pins, tighten the connector screws, and test with a higher-quality cable.

definition: dongles or converters that allow a device to connect to a monitor using a different interface
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Signal not detected or resolution issues.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the adapter is an 'active' adapter if required, check for firmware updates for the adapter, and verify input/output settings.

definition: the physical wires used to carry video signals from a computer to a monitor
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Distorted picture, no signal, or incorrect colors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Swap the cable, try a different port, and ensure the monitor is set to the correct signal source.

definition: a virtualized computer environment that runs on physical host hardware using a hypervisor
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Slow performance, networking issues, or VM failing to boot.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check host resource allocation (CPU/RAM), verify the virtual network switch configuration, and update the hypervisor software.

definition: a network that uses physical cabling like ethernet to connect devices
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Network cable unplugged' or connection latency.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the physical link lights on the NIC and switch port, test with a known-good cable, and verify IP configuration.

definition: networks that use radio frequency to connect devices
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Weak signal, inability to connect, or high packet loss.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Move closer to the access point, remove physical obstructions, and ensure the correct security key is used.

definition: an isp that provides internet access using wireless technology instead of traditional cables
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Intermittent connectivity or weather-related outages.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the antenna alignment for clear line-of-sight to the WISP tower and restart the radio receiver equipment.

definition: a control flow statement for code iteration that allows code to be executed repeatedly based on a boolean condition or a specific sequence
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Script hangs due to an infinite loop, or the script processes the wrong number of data items.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Add debugging statements (e.g., “echo” commands) within the loop to track variable values and ensure the loop condition eventually evaluates to false.

definition: a conditional statement that performs different actions depending on whether a programmer-specified boolean condition evaluates to true or false
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The script takes the wrong branch of execution, or errors occur when the condition evaluates to an unexpected state.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the syntax of the conditional expression and use a debugger or print statements to confirm the variables being compared hold the expected values before the statement is evaluated.

definition: replaceable components required for a printer to function such as toner cartridges ink cartridges paper and transfer belts
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Faded print, "Low Toner" or "Low Ink" warnings on the display, or paper jams caused by worn rollers.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the printer's maintenance menu or web interface for supply levels, replace depleted consumables with manufacturer-recommended parts, and perform a calibration or cleaning cycle if necessary.

definition: a form of operating system os virtualization where the kernel allows for multiple isolated user-space instances containers to run on a single host
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The container fails to start, resource starvation occurs on the host, or network connectivity between containers is lost.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use commands such as “docker ps” to check the status, inspect container logs with “docker logs [container_id]”, and verify that host resources (CPU (Central Processing Unit) and RAM (Random Access Memory)) are not fully consumed.

definition: stages of an ir incident response plan containment stops the spread of an attack eradication removes the threat and recovery restores the system to a clean state
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Malware spreading across the network, unauthorized users remaining in the system, or data continuing to be exfiltrated.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Follow the established IR policy: physically disconnect infected machines, change compromised credentials, re-image systems from known-good backups, and run anti-malware scans to ensure the threat is gone.

definition: a security feature that restricts access to specific websites or types of content often managed at the router or os level
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users cannot access legitimate websites, or restricted content is still being displayed.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the filter’s blocklist/allowlist, verify that the correct user account policy is applied, and update the software database used for content categorization.

definition: a tab within the windows internet options utility used for managing certificates auto-complete settings and feeds
ERROR SYMPTOMS: SSL (Secure Sockets Layer)/TLS (Transport Layer Security) connection errors, or inability to manage saved web forms.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Access the tab through the Control Panel, click “Certificates” to inspect or import missing root authorities, or click “AutoComplete” settings to manage stored data.

definition: a legacy section of the windows operating system that provides centralized access to system settings hardware management and user configurations
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Settings cannot be modified, or applets fail to open, indicating corruption in the system configuration.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the Control Panel by typing “control” in the Run dialog or search bar; if an applet fails to launch, verify the system files using the “sfc /scannow” command.

definition: a windows applet used to view manage and troubleshoot connected hardware peripherals including printers scanners and input devices
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Device status shows as "Offline" or "Driver unavailable."
TROUBLESHOOTING: Right-click the problematic device, select “Troubleshoot” to run the automated diagnostic, or go to “Printer Properties” to verify ports and driver installation.

definition: a collection of settings in windows designed to assist users with visual hearing or physical impairments
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Accessibility features like Narrator or High Contrast mode activating unexpectedly.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Navigate to the “Ease of Access” center in the Control Panel and disable unwanted features or toggle the “Keyboard shortcut” settings to prevent accidental activation.

definition: a window that allows users to change how files and folders are viewed hidden and indexed within the windows file system
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Cannot view file extensions or hidden files that are necessary for troubleshooting.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “File Explorer Options” via the Control Panel, click the “View” tab, and check “Show hidden files, folders, and drives” or uncheck “Hide extensions for known file types”.

definition: a service that tracks the location of files to speed up search results within the operating system
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Searches in the Start menu or File Explorer are slow or fail to return expected results.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Indexing Options” in the Control Panel, click “Advanced”, and select “Rebuild” to refresh the search database.

definition: a centralized utility for configuring browser-related settings proxy servers and security zones
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Browsers failing to load pages or showing security errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Internet Options”, go to the “Advanced” tab, and click “Restore advanced settings” or “Reset” the browser configurations.

definition: a specific applet usually mail microsoft outlook used to configure profiles email accounts and data files for microsoft outlook
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Outlook fails to connect to the mail server, or the profile is corrupted.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the “Mail” applet in the Control Panel, click “Show Profiles”, and create a new profile to see if the connection issues persist.

definition: settings that control how the computer uses energy including sleep hibernation and performance modes
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Computer goes to sleep too quickly, fails to wake, or does not maintain performance during heavy tasks.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Power Options” in the Control Panel, choose a plan (e.g., “High Performance”), and adjust the “Change plan settings” to match the user's needs.

definition: a tool that forces older applications to run in a mode simulating a previous version of windows
ERROR SYMPTOMS: An application crashes upon launch on a newer version of Windows.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Right-click the application shortcut, select “Properties”, go to the “Compatibility” tab, and check “Run this program in compatibility mode for” while selecting the appropriate Windows version.

definition: a utility used to install uninstall or modify software and windows features
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Cannot remove a buggy application or need to enable a Windows component (like SMB (Server Message Block)).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Programs and Features”, select the application to “Uninstall/Change”, or click “Turn Windows features on or off” to modify OS components.

definition: a utility to manage audio devices including input microphone and output speakers settings
ERROR SYMPTOMS: No sound from speakers, or the microphone is not being picked up by applications.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the “Sound” applet, check the “Playback” and “Recording” tabs, and ensure the correct device is set as the “Default Device”.

definition: a section for managing local user accounts passwords and account types standard vs administrator
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Cannot change user passwords or lack of administrative privileges to perform system tasks.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the “User Accounts” applet in the Control Panel to modify account settings; if locked out, you may need to boot into “Safe Mode” to use the built-in Administrator account.

definition: a broad term for the various administrative applets available in the control panel that help manage configure and monitor windows
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Inability to perform administrative tasks, pointing to missing or damaged system utilities.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the Control Panel in “Large icons” or “Small icons” view to see all available utilities, and use them to perform standard configuration and troubleshooting tasks.

definition: while windows 10 relies heavily on the settings app the classic control panel still exists to provide granular control over advanced legacy settings
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Settings are not visible in the new “Settings” app.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Search for “Control Panel” in the Windows search bar to access the classic utility for advanced configurations not found in the modern UI.

definition: a host-based firewall that controls network traffic to and from a single workstation
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Applications cannot communicate over the network, or ports seem blocked.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Windows Defender Firewall” in the Control Panel, click “Allow an app or feature through Windows Defender Firewall”, and verify the application is listed and enabled.

definition: expansion cards typically pcie peripheral component interconnect express that provide additional interfaces for storage like sata or raid redundant array of independent disks or connectivity
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Attached storage or peripherals are not detected by the OS, or the system fails to boot.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the card is firmly seated in the PCIe slot, install the necessary device drivers, and check the BIOS/UEFI settings to ensure the slot is enabled.

definition: system messages indicating that a usb controller is overloaded or lacks the necessary bandwidth to support connected devices
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A pop-up message stating “USB controller resources exceeded” or devices disconnecting frequently.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Remove high-bandwidth devices (like webcams or external drives) from the same USB hub, or add a secondary USB controller card to distribute the load.

definition: mechanisms used to remove heat from the processor including heat sinks fans and liquid cooling systems
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The system shuts down unexpectedly due to thermal throttling or "CPU Over Temperature" errors during boot.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the fan is spinning, ensure the heat sink is properly mounted, clean dust from the fins, and reapply thermal paste if necessary.

definition: active cooling components used to move air across heat sinks or through the computer case to dissipate heat
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Excessive noise (grinding/clicking), fans not spinning, or system overheating.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Inspect the fan for physical obstructions, clean dust from the blades, and replace the fan if it is failing to spin or producing abnormal noises.

definition: the process of identifying and resolving thermal issues that lead to system instability crashes or component damage
ERROR SYMPTOMS: BSOD (Blue Screen of Death), sudden power-offs, or loud fan speeds.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use hardware monitoring software (like “HWMonitor”) to check temperatures, ensure proper airflow (cable management), and verify that all cooling fans are functional.

definition: a command-line instruction cmd exe used to duplicate files from one location to another
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Access denied or "File not found" errors during file transfer.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check that the source file exists and that the user has sufficient permissions for both the source and the destination directories.

definition: the process of creating a replica of data files in a different directory or drive
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Files fail to copy due to permission issues or insufficient disk space.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify disk space, check for “Read-Only” file attributes, and ensure the user has “Write” permissions on the target directory.

definition: the process of replicating an entire directory and its contents to a new destination
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Incomplete transfers or "Access Denied" for files inside the folder.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the source path is correct and consider using more robust commands like “xcopy” or “robocopy” if advanced file attributes (like permissions) need to be preserved.

definition: a scenario where a user's windows profile becomes damaged preventing login or causing desktop settings and files to disappear
ERROR SYMPTOMS: User Profile Service failed the logon error message, or a temporary profile is loaded instead of the user's custom environment.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Boot into “Safe Mode”, rename the corrupted profile folder in “C:\Users”, delete the corresponding SID (Security Identifier) in the Registry Editor (“regedit”), and then have the user log in again to recreate the profile.

definition: crucial operating system files that have been damaged or deleted leading to system instability or failure to boot
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Boot loops, system crashes, or Windows features failing to launch.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Run the “System File Checker” by executing the command “sfc /scannow” in an elevated command prompt to automatically find and repair system files.

definition: the effective range and signal strength of a wi-fi wireless fidelity signal based on the frequency band 2 4 ghz vs 5 ghz 6 ghz and the environment
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Wi-Fi signal is weak or drops out in certain areas of the building.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Install additional wireless access points, use signal extenders, or switch to a frequency with better range (2.4 GHz) if the signal is being blocked by walls.

definition: a cli instruction in linux and macos used to copy files and directories
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Permission denied or "Command not found" if the utility is missing or the path is incorrect.
TROUBLESHOOTING: If a file cannot be copied, use “sudo cp” to run the command with administrative privileges; check that the source and destination paths are correct.

definition: the primary component of a computer that performs most of the processing inside the computer acting as the brain
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System failure to POST (Power-On Self-Test), random reboots, or system freezes under load.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify proper seating in the socket, check for bent pins, ensure sufficient cooling is applied, and check BIOS settings to confirm the CPU is correctly detected.

definition: a cpu architecture that can address up to 4 gb gigabytes of ram and processes data in 32-bit chunks
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System cannot access more than 4 GB of RAM, or 64-bit software fails to install.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Confirm the hardware supports a 64-bit CPU if more memory is required; 32-bit CPUs are legacy and cannot be upgraded to run 64-bit code.

definition: a cpu architecture that can address significantly more than 4 gb of ram and processes data in 64-bit chunks allowing for better performance
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Reduced performance if a 32-bit OS is installed on 64-bit hardware.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the operating system installed is 64-bit to fully utilize the CPU's capabilities and memory addressing.

definition: a line of processors developed by amd advanced micro devices
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Boot failures or incompatibility with specific motherboard sockets.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the CPU model is supported by the motherboard's socket (e.g., AM4, AM5) and ensure the BIOS is updated to support the specific processor architecture.

definition: an architecture based on risc reduced instruction set computer design primarily used in mobile devices and energy-efficient laptops
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Incompatibility with standard x86 software.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use ARM-compatible software or emulation layers provided by the operating system to run legacy applications.

definition: small high-speed memory located on or near the cpu that stores frequently accessed data to reduce latency
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System performs significantly slower than expected for its specifications.
TROUBLESHOOTING: If cache errors are suspected, check for CPU hardware damage; cache issues usually cannot be fixed by software and require a CPU replacement.

definition: the speed at which a processor executes instructions measured in ghz
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System runs slower than advertised clock speeds.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check BIOS for “power-saving” features that may be downclocking the CPU or for “thermal throttling” caused by insufficient cooling.

definition: ensuring the cpu is supported by the motherboard's socket and chipset
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System will not boot, or the CPU is not identified by the motherboard.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Consult the motherboard manufacturer’s “CPU Support List” on their website to ensure the specific CPU version and stepping are compatible.

definition: active or passive thermal management required to prevent cpu overheating
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Sudden system shutdowns or thermal throttling.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Clean dust from the heat sink, ensure the fan header is connected, and verify thermal paste coverage between the CPU and heat sink.

definition: a sudden flow of electricity between two electrically charged objects which can permanently damage sensitive cpu pins or internal circuits
ERROR SYMPTOMS: CPU fails immediately upon installation.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Wear an ESD strap or touch the metal case of the computer before handling the CPU to prevent static damage; there is no fix for a CPU damaged by ESD.

definition: a processor designed specifically to handle graphical computations sometimes integrated into the cpu die
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Visual artifacts, slow frame rates, or no display output.
TROUBLESHOOTING: If using integrated graphics, ensure the drivers are updated; if using a dedicated GPU, check for proper seating and power cable connection.

definition: the physical process of placing the processor into the motherboard socket
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System does not boot; bent pins or improper alignment.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Remove the CPU, inspect the pins on the socket or CPU, align the “golden triangle” on the CPU with the socket, and lock the retention arm.

definition: a line of processors developed by intel
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Incompatibility if placed in an AMD-specific socket.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Confirm the CPU is compatible with the Intel motherboard socket (e.g., LGA 1700) before installation.

definition: a processor with two or more independent cores that allow it to process multiple threads of data simultaneously
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Poor multitasking performance.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the OS and applications are correctly detecting all cores; check BIOS settings to ensure no cores have been manually disabled.

definition: a technology like intel's hyper-threading that allows a single core to act as two logical processors to improve efficiency
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Programs designed to use multiple threads run slowly if multithreading is disabled.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Enter the BIOS/UEFI and verify that “Hyper-Threading” or “Simultaneous Multithreading” (SMT) is enabled.

definition: increasing the cpu's clock rate beyond the manufacturer's rated speed
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System instability, BSODs, or permanent CPU damage due to excessive heat/voltage.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Revert BIOS settings to “Load Optimized Defaults” to restore factory clock speeds.

definition: the amount of electrical power measured in watts w the cpu requires during operation
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Sudden system shutdown under heavy load (PSU (Power Supply Unit) overload).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the PSU has enough wattage to support the CPU's TDP (Thermal Design Power) and all other components.

definition: the physical interface on the motherboard where the cpu is mounted
ERROR SYMPTOMS: CPU does not fit, or the retention mechanism will not close.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the motherboard and CPU socket types match exactly before attempting installation.

definition: using stress-testing software to verify the cpu is stable under high workloads
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System crashes or errors (e.g., “Prime95” errors) during a stability test.
TROUBLESHOOTING: If stability tests fail, reduce overclock settings, improve cooling, or consider replacing a faulty CPU.

definition: diagnosing issues related to processor performance temperature or compatibility
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Boot failures, system hangs, or thermal errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Monitor temperatures, update the BIOS, check for CPU installation errors, and perform hardware diagnostics to rule out other components.

definition: the electrical potential supplied to the cpu for operation
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Instability, or the system fails to boot if the voltage is too low or too high.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the motherboard is automatically setting the CPU voltage correctly or adjust manually in BIOS if overclocking.

definition: a common synonym for 64-bit cpu architecture
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unable to run 64-bit software.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the OS is 64-bit; verify the CPU supports x64 instructions (most modern CPUs do).

definition: a likely typo for x86 32-bit cpu architecture
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System errors or software compatibility issues.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Correctly identify the CPU architecture; x86 refers to 32-bit architecture.

definition: the process of attempting to recover a password from stored data such as a hashed password file using automated tools to guess the password
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Security audits identifying weak password hashes, or evidence of unauthorized access using stolen credentials.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Enforce strong, complex password policies, implement MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication), and use slow hashing algorithms (like “bcrypt”) to make offline cracking attempts computationally expensive.

definition: a state where an application unexpectedly terminates stops responding or closes due to software bugs memory errors or os operating system conflicts
ERROR SYMPTOMS: “Application not responding” dialogs, unexpected program exits, or “Event Viewer” logs showing “Application Error” entries.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check “Event Viewer” for error codes, update the application to the latest version, verify system file integrity using “sfc /scannow”, or reinstall the application.

definition: a twisted-pair ethernet cable where the transmit and receive wire pairs are swapped at one end traditionally used to connect two similar devices like switch-to-switch or pc-to-pc directly
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Link lights failing to illuminate or no data transmission between two directly connected devices that do not support Auto-MDIX (Medium Dependent Interface Crossover).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use a standard straight-through cable if both devices support Auto-MDIX, or verify that the cable is indeed a “crossover” type using a cable tester.

definition: a virtualization technique that allows a guest operating system to run on a host system with a different architecture or os
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Guest OS fails to boot, or performance is severely degraded due to inefficient emulation.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the hypervisor (like “VirtualBox” or “QEMU”) supports the specific guest architecture, and verify that hardware-assisted virtualization (like “VT-x” or “AMD-V”) is enabled in the BIOS/UEFI.

definition: a web security vulnerability where an attacker injects malicious client-side scripts into a web page viewed by other users
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users seeing strange pop-ups on legitimate sites, or unauthorized actions being performed on behalf of a user.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Developers must implement input sanitization and output encoding to ensure user-supplied data cannot be executed as scripts by the browser.

definition: legacy display technology that uses electron guns to illuminate a phosphor-coated screen these units contain high-voltage capacitors that can hold a charge long after the power is unplugged
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Monitor not turning on, or user suffering a severe shock when opening the casing.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Never open a CRT monitor casing unless you have been trained in high-voltage safety; if the monitor is faulty, it is recommended to recycle the entire unit safely.

definition: methods used to find weaknesses in a cryptographic system such as brute-forcing side-channel attacks or frequency analysis
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Encrypted data being decrypted without the key, or sudden system compromises.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use robust, industry-standard encryption protocols (like “AES-256”) and frequently rotate keys to minimize the window of opportunity for cryptanalysis.

definition: a hardware device or software utility that generates one-time passwords or stores digital certificates for authentication mfa
ERROR SYMPTOMS: User cannot log in because the token is not synchronized or the battery is dead.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Resynchronize the token with the authentication server or replace the token if it is hardware-defective.

definition: malicious software that uses a victim's hardware resources cpu gpu to mine cryptocurrencies without the owner's consent
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Extremely high CPU (Central Processing Unit) usage, loud fan noise, or system sluggishness even when no heavy applications are open.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Scan the system with reputable anti-malware software, check the “Task Manager” for suspicious background processes, and remove the malware.

definition: an issue with input devices like a mouse or stylus where the cursor moves across the screen without user interaction
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The mouse pointer is jittery or moves on its own while the user is not touching the device.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Clean the surface, ensure the sensor is free of debris, update the driver, or test the device on a different computer to rule out hardware failure.

definition: the documented record of evidence or sensitive equipment ensuring it has remained secure and untampered with from collection to analysis
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Evidence being ruled inadmissible in an investigation due to lack of proper documentation.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Always maintain a physical or digital log that records who collected the item, where it was stored, and who accessed it at every step of the process.

definition: tools specifically designed to cleanly cut through various types of communication cabling without crushing the internal wires
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Poor network connectivity caused by frayed or shorted wires due to improper cutting.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use professional-grade cable cutters rather than household scissors to ensure a clean, flush cut that allows for proper termination.

definition: a publicly accessible list of known cybersecurity vulnerabilities providing a standardized identifier for each threat
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Security scanners flagging systems as vulnerable.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Research the specific CVE ID in the database to understand the threat, then apply the recommended software patches or configuration changes to mitigate the vulnerability.

definition: an early impact printing technology that uses a wheel with characters at the end of spokes to strike an inked ribbon against paper
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Faded characters, stuck spokes, or extremely slow printing speeds.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Clean the wheel, replace the ink ribbon, and ensure the hammer mechanism is moving freely; however, consider upgrading as this technology is obsolete.

definition: a failure of the physical keys controller or internal membrane of a keyboard
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Specific keys not working, multiple characters appearing when one key is pressed, or the keyboard not being detected.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Clean the keyboard, check the physical connection (USB (Universal Serial Bus) or Bluetooth), update/reinstall the keyboard driver, or replace the hardware.

definition: mobile hardware smartphones or tablets that has sustained physical damage e g screen cracks or security compromises e g rootkits
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Screen flicker, rapid battery drain, or unauthorized app behavior.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Perform a factory reset, check for unauthorized apps, and inspect for physical damage; replace the battery or screen if needed.

definition: the act of removing cached web pages cookies history and stored form data to protect privacy or fix loading issues
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Old versions of websites loading, or privacy concerns regarding local data storage.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the browser’s settings, navigate to “Privacy and Security”, and select “Clear browsing data” to remove temporary files.

definition: configuring an os to prevent it from automatically sending telemetry or usage data to the vendor
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Excessive network traffic or privacy concerns.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Access the “Settings” app, go to “Privacy”, and toggle off “Diagnostics & feedback” or similar telemetry options.

definition: the secure permanent removal of data from storage media to ensure it cannot be recovered
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Sensitive data found on decommissioned hard drives.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use “shredding” software for magnetic media, “degaussing” for hard drives, or physically pulverizing the media to ensure total destruction.

definition: a set of security standards designed to ensure that all companies that accept process store or transmit credit card information maintain a secure environment
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Compliance audit failures.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Implement strict access controls, encrypt transmitted card data, and regularly test security systems to meet “PCI-DSS” requirements.

definition: securing the physical locations and devices where data resides such as locked server rooms or cable locks on laptops
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Theft of physical storage devices (USB drives, external HDDs).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Implement physical access controls like cages, safes, and surveillance cameras to protect hardware.

definition: the process of restoring data from backups after a security incident such as a ransomware infection
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data encrypted by ransomware or system unusable.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Isolate infected systems, verify the backup is clean, and restore data only after the environment has been successfully sanitized.

definition: information protected by law or organizational policy e g pii personally identifiable information phi protected health information
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Accidental disclosure or data leak.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Apply strict encryption at rest and in transit, and strictly limit access based on the “Principle of Least Privilege”.

definition: the overarching practice of protecting data from unauthorized access corruption or theft
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unauthorized access or data breach incidents.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Implement a layered defense strategy including firewalls, encryption, backups, and regular audits.

definition: the process of configuring folder permissions and network settings to allow other users on a lan local area network to access files
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users getting an “Access Denied” error when trying to map a network drive.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Right-click the folder, select “Properties”, go to the “Sharing” tab, and configure proper “Permissions” for the desired user groups.

definition: the process of syncing user settings bookmarks and passwords across multiple devices using a cloud account like a microsoft account
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data not updating across devices, or sign-in errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure both devices are logged into the same account, verify internet connectivity, and check the “Sync” settings menu to ensure data types are enabled.

definition: a basic data type that represents whole numbers without decimals
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Script or program error when a non-integer value is provided to a function expecting an integer.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use type-casting functions in the script to ensure the input data is correctly converted to the expected integer format.

definition: a sequence of characters used to represent text
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Program errors when math is attempted on string variables.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure variables are declared correctly and that strings are properly enclosed in quotes within the script.

definition: the port on a laptop where the power adapter connects it is a common point of failure for power issues
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Laptop power cuts out when the cable is moved, or the battery doesn’t charge.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Inspect the jack for physical damage or loose connections; if faulty, this often requires soldering or replacing the power board component.

definition: a powerful cli tool in linux macos used to copy and convert raw data often used for creating disk images or securely wiping drives
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data corruption or accidental deletion if the wrong target device is specified.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Double-check the command syntax (especially the “if” and “of” parameters) and verify the target device identifier before execution.

definition: an attack where multiple compromised systems flood a target server with traffic making it unavailable
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Server timeout or website unavailable.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use a cloud-based “DDoS” protection service to filter malicious traffic and block the source IP addresses.

definition: a type of synchronous dynamic ram sdram that transfers data on both the rising and falling edges of the clock signal doubling the speed
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System boot failure or beep codes indicating memory issues.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Reseat the RAM module, clean the contacts, or test the module in a different slot.

definition: a generation of ddr memory that operates at higher speeds and lower voltages than its predecessors
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Incompatibility error when trying to install in a DDR4/DDR5 slot.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the motherboard specifically supports DDR3, as notches on the module prevent installation into incompatible slots.

definition: a high-performance generation of memory that replaced ddr3 offering higher clock speeds and lower power consumption
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System hang or boot errors if the motherboard does not support DDR4.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify motherboard compatibility and ensure the modules are properly seated in the DIMM (Dual-Inline Memory Module) slot.

definition: the latest high-speed generation of memory featuring improved power efficiency and increased density
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Boot failure if the motherboard is designed for DDR4.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify BIOS/UEFI firmware supports DDR5 and ensure the memory is compatible with the CPU/motherboard combo.

definition: the essential security practice of replacing manufacturer-set passwords like admin admin upon installation
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unauthorized access to devices (like routers) due to well-known default credentials.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Access the device settings and update the administrator password to a complex, unique string immediately upon deployment.

definition: a windows utility used to reorganize fragmented data on hdd hard disk drive media to improve performance
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Slow file access or system sluggishness.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open a command prompt as administrator and run “defrag c:” to optimize disk layout.

definition: the process of moving file pieces together on a mechanical hard drive so they are stored contiguously
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Slow system performance when launching apps.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the Windows “Optimize Drives” tool or run “defrag” from the command line; do not defrag SSDs (Solid State Drives) as it is unnecessary and increases wear.

definition: a cli instruction used in windows to delete one or more files
ERROR SYMPTOMS: “Access Denied” error if the file is in use or protected.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Close the application using the file or use “del /f” to force deletion of read-only files.

definition: various versions of linux like ubuntu fedora that provide a graphical user interface for desktop users
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Inability to run standard Windows software or driver issues for custom hardware.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use package managers (like “apt” or “dnf”) to install supported software, or use WINE (Wine Is Not an Emulator) to run Windows apps.

definition: a protocol that allows a user to connect to another computer over a network and view its graphical desktop
ERROR SYMPTOMS: “Remote Desktop” connection failures.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the host computer has “Remote Desktop” enabled in settings and that the firewall allows traffic on port “3389”.

definition: a feature that enables a user to control a remote computer as if they were sitting in front of it
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Lag or connection timeout.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify network stability, check that the host machine is awake, and confirm the port is not blocked.

definition: replacing a physical computer or virtual desktop environment when hardware is obsolete or fails
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System failure or inability to run modern software.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Assess hardware requirements, back up all necessary user data, and migrate the data to the new machine.

definition: keeping files settings current across multiple machines
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Files missing on one device.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Re-authenticate the synchronization account and verify the network connection.

definition: a popular linux-based desktop distribution known for ease of use
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Software installation issues.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the “Terminal” to run “sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade” to resolve software dependency issues.

definition: running a virtual desktop vdi virtual desktop infrastructure or local vm virtual machine
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Virtual desktop performance issues or host resource depletion.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Increase allocated RAM and CPU cores in the hypervisor settings, and check network latency for VDI solutions.

definition: the modern microsoft operating system successor to windows 10
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Compatibility issues with older software or hardware.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use “Compatibility Mode” in properties, or update drivers to the latest versions.

definition: the primary user interface of the windows os
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Desktop icons not showing or wallpaper/theme issues.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Right-click the desktop and ensure “Show desktop icons” is checked; check “Personalization” settings for display issues.

definition: the secure permanent removal of data from storage media
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data breach due to improper disposal.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Destroy the media (crush, shred) or use specialized software to overwrite the disk multiple times.

definition: ensuring that chemicals batteries and hardware are disposed of according to local environmental regulations like weee waste electrical and electronic equipment directives
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Legal non-compliance or environmental damage.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use certified e-waste recycling centers and follow manufacturer guidelines for battery disposal.

definition: the stage in the incident response process where an incident is identified validated and analyzed to determine its scope
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Security alerts in “SIEM” (Security Information and Event Management) logs.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Review logs, interview users, and perform packet analysis to determine if the alert is a true positive incident.

definition: programs like apple developer or microsoft dev that provide tools sdks software development kits and documentation for software creation
ERROR SYMPTOMS: SDKs not installing or failing to compile code.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify OS version meets the minimum requirements, install required dependencies, and check for conflicting software.

definition: problems with hardware drivers or hardware functionality
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Device not recognized or marked with a yellow exclamation mark in “Device Manager”.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Reinstall drivers via “Device Manager”, check cables, or swap the device to test functionality.

definition: a windows utility used to view and manage hardware drivers and settings
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Hardware not working or “Code 10/43” driver errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Device Manager”, right-click the hardware, and select “Update driver” or “Uninstall device” to trigger a refresh.

definition: a legacy windows applet for managing peripheral hardware
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Printer won't print or scanner not found.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Devices and Printers”, right-click the device, and check the “Printer Properties” or “Troubleshoot” option.

definition: the modern windows location windows 10 11 to manage bluetooth printers and mouse settings
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Device not pairing or settings not saving.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Navigate to “Settings > Devices” (or “Bluetooth & devices” in Win11) and toggle the device off/on, or remove and re-pair it.

definition: a linux macos cli utility used to display available disk space on file systems
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System "disk full" error.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Run “df -h” to view partition usage in a human-readable format and identify which partition is full.

definition: a network protocol that automatically assigns ip internet protocol addresses and other network parameters to clients
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Clients unable to connect to the network (“No Internet Access”).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Run “ipconfig /renew” on the client, or check the “DHCP” server scope to ensure addresses are available.

definition: the four-step dhcp handshake discover offer request acknowledge
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Client receives an “APIPA” (Automatic Private IP Addressing) address (169.254.x.x) instead of a valid IP.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Analyze packet captures (“Wireshark”) to see which stage of the “DORA” process is failing, then check network connectivity to the server.

definition: a feature where a dhcp server permanently assigns a specific ip address to a client based on its mac media access control address
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Network conflicts or application connection failures.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the “MAC” address of the device matches the reservation on the “DHCP” server.

definition: the range of ip addresses that a dhcp server is configured to lease to clients
ERROR SYMPTOMS: New clients cannot join the network because the scope is exhausted.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Increase the “DHCP” scope range or shorten the lease times on the server.

definition: a network device or server service that manages the ip address pool
ERROR SYMPTOMS: All clients on the network lose connectivity.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the “DHCP” server service is running and that the server has a static IP address.

definition: a legacy connection that uses a modem and an analog phone line to connect to the internet
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Very slow speeds or line noise interference.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the phone line connection and that the modem is correctly configured in “Device Manager”.

definition: a password attack that uses a pre-generated list of common words or phrases to guess a password
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Multiple failed login attempts in system logs.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Implement account lockout policies after a number of failed attempts to block automated dictionary tools.

definition: a backup strategy that only copies files that have changed since the last full backup
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Long backup times or restore failures.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the schedule and ensure there is enough space on the backup media for both the “Full” backup and the growing “Differential” backups.

definition: a cli utility used to query dns domain name system name servers for information
ERROR SYMPTOMS: “DNS” resolution errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Run “dig [domainname]” to see if the DNS server is correctly resolving the domain to an IP address.

definition: a hardware layer that sits on top of a display to detect touch input
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Screen ignores touch input or registers phantom touches.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Clean the screen, calibrate the touch interface in settings, or check for physical damage.

definition: the standard physical form factor for ram used in desktop computers
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System won't post if the DIMM is not seated.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the locking clips on the “DIMM” slot click into place when installing.

definition: a cli command in windows to list files and directories
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Command not found or insufficient directory access.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Navigate to the correct directory first using “cd” before running “dir”.

definition: cabling specifically designed to be buried directly in the ground without the need for conduit
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Network failure due to water ingress or cable crushing.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the cable is rated for “direct burial”; if it fails, test for continuity and look for signs of physical disturbance or moisture damage.

definition: a logical structure for organizing files in a file system
ERROR SYMPTOMS: “File not found” due to files being in the wrong directory.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the “dir” command to view the file system structure and navigate using “cd”.

definition: microsoft s directory service used for network management and user authentication
ERROR SYMPTOMS: User login failures or group policy not applying.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify network connectivity to the “Domain Controller” and ensure the client computer’s time is synced with the domain.

definition: a cli command to change the current working directory
ERROR SYMPTOMS: “System cannot find the path specified”.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Type the correct path or use “cd ..” to move up one directory level.

definition: cli utility to copy files
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Access denied.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Run the command prompt as an administrator.

definition: cli utility to delete files
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Cannot delete file.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the file is not marked as “Read-Only”.

definition: cli utility to list files
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Listing not showing expected files.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use “dir /a” to show hidden files.

definition: a protocol used to access and maintain distributed directory information services
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Failed authentication in corporate applications.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the “LDAP” server address, port (default 389/636), and bind credentials.

definition: cli command to create make a new directory
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Directory already exists.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Choose a unique name or rename the existing directory.

definition: cli command to remove a directory
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Directory not empty.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use “rd /s” to remove the directory and all subdirectories/files.

definition: robust file copy command designed for reliable copying of large directory trees
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Copying fails on long paths or locked files.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use “robocopy” with flags like “/mir” or “/r:0” for better stability in scripts.

definition: the hierarchical organization of the file system
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Lost files or inability to save files.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use a file explorer or the “tree” command to visualize and repair directory hierarchies.

definition: a cli utility to display the directory structure in a graphical tree format
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Confusion regarding folder hierarchy.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Run “tree /f” to see all directories and files within them.

definition: a legacy cli tool to copy files and directory trees
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Incomplete copy of large structures.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the “/e” or “/s” flags are used to copy subdirectories.

definition: a windows feature that automatically executes applications or opens folders when removable media such as usb drives or cds are inserted disabling it is a security best practice to prevent the automatic execution of malicious software
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Security alerts regarding unauthorized program execution or the unexpected appearance of windows/folders upon connecting external storage.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Navigate to “Settings > Bluetooth & devices > AutoPlay” and toggle the “Use AutoPlay for all media and devices” setting to “Off”.

definition: a windows legacy feature that reads the autorun inf file on a drive to determine how to launch a program or install an application disabling this is critical to prevent malware from launching automatically upon media insertion
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Malware infections originating from external storage devices immediately upon being plugged into a computer port.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “gpedit.msc” (Group Policy Editor), navigate to “Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > AutoRun Policies”, and set “Turn off AutoPlay” to “Enabled”.

definition: the practice of turning off background telemetry and diagnostic data transmission features in an os that monitor user activity hardware health and software usage for the vendor
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Higher than expected background network bandwidth consumption and privacy concerns regarding unauthorized data sharing.
TROUBLESHOOTING: In Windows, go to “Settings > Privacy & security > Diagnostics & feedback” and set diagnostic data to “Required diagnostic data only” or disable optional data tracking.

definition: the act of deactivating the default limited-privilege guest user account that exists in many operating systems which can otherwise be used by unauthorized parties to gain a foothold on the system
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unauthorized access to the local machine without a password, or security auditing tools flagging guest accounts as an active vulnerability.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Computer Management” (compmgmt.msc), navigate to “Local Users and Groups > Users”, right-click the “Guest” account, select “Properties”, and check the “Account is disabled” box.

definition: a hardware-level security measure where specific physical ports e g usb ethernet are physically blocked or disabled via the bios uefi basic input output system unified extensible firmware interface to prevent unauthorized devices from connecting to the system
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Peripheral devices (like keyboards, mice, or drives) failing to function when plugged into specific ports despite the devices being verified as working.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Enter the BIOS/UEFI setup menu during boot, navigate to “Advanced” or “Integrated Peripherals”, locate the specific port setting (e.g., USB Controller), and change the setting to “Disabled”.

definition: the act of configuring a wireless router to stop broadcasting the network name ssid while not a true security measure it hides the network from casual wi-fi scanners
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Wireless devices unable to discover the network in the list of available Wi-Fi connections, necessitating manual connection configuration.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Log in to the wireless router’s web-based administration interface, navigate to the “Wireless” settings, and uncheck the “Enable SSID Broadcast” or “Visible” box.

definition: a process where the system-wide capability to revert the operating system to a previous state using snapshots restore points is deactivated to free up disk space or secure the system state
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Inability to roll back system changes, missing restore points, or an inability to boot into the recovery console for troubleshooting.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Search for “Create a restore point” in the taskbar, select the system drive, click “Configure”, and select “Disable system protection”.

definition: the process of preventing the operating system from collecting and sending usage statistics and error logs to the manufacturer's servers
