TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the drive is formatted correctly, use the “Disk Management” tool to assign a drive letter, or—if mounting a virtual disk—right-click the file and select “Mount” to create a temporary logical drive.

definition: a maintenance task that helps a drive perform more efficiently for hdds this means defragmentation for ssds this means the trim command which helps the drive manage free space
ERROR SYMPTOMS: General system sluggishness over time.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Defragment and Optimize Drives”, verify the system correctly identifies the drive type (HDD vs SSD), and run the optimization tool to ensure the operating system is performing the correct housekeeping tasks (Defrag for HDD, TRIM for SSD).

definition: a data sanitization method where new random or fixed data like zeros is written over existing data on every addressable sector of a storage device
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Improperly overwritten data could potentially be recovered by advanced forensic software if only a single pass is used.
TROUBLESHOOTING: To ensure data is unrecoverable, use a software tool that performs multiple passes of data overwriting, or verify the drive’s security documentation to see if it supports a "Secure Erase" feature at the controller level.

definition: a robust sanitization process that makes data recovery infeasible using state-of-the-art laboratory techniques often achieved through cryptographic erasure if the drive was encrypted or multiple overwrite passes
ERROR SYMPTOMS: N/A (Proactive security measure).
TROUBLESHOOTING: If using cryptographic erasure, delete the encryption keys; if using overwriting, use software that satisfies NIST 800-88 standards for purging, which ensures that even specialized recovery equipment cannot restore the original data.

definition: redundant array of independent disks raid is a technology that uses multiple hard drives in combination to provide data redundancy improve performance or both e g raid 0 1 5 10
ERROR SYMPTOMS: RAID array degraded warnings, data corruption, or total volume loss if the number of drive failures exceeds the parity or mirroring limits.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Access the RAID controller’s BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) or software management console, identify the failed drive, replace it with an identical component, and initiate a "rebuild" of the array.

definition: the physical process of removing a faulty or obsolete storage device and installing a new unit
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Hardware diagnostic tools indicate irreparable sector failure or total mechanical death.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Back up all data, shut down the system, remove the chassis side panel, disconnect power and data cables, unscrew the drive from its mounting bay, insert the new drive, reconnect all cables, and install the operating system/restore data.

definition: a process meant to render access to target data on the media infeasible for a given level of effort this encompasses clearing purging or destroying the drive
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Insecure media disposal causing potential information leakage.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Choose the sanitization method appropriate for the data sensitivity level (e.g., clearing is sufficient for low-sensitivity data; destruction is required for top-secret data) and maintain a certification log for compliance.

definition: a storage interface serial advanced technology attachment used to connect hard drives and optical drives to the motherboard supporting data transfer rates up to 6 gigabits per second gbps for sata iii
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Intermittent drive connection, "Drive not found" errors, or system freezes due to bad SATA cables.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Replace the SATA data cable with a known-good one, try a different SATA port on the motherboard, and ensure the power supply is delivering stable voltage to the drive connector.

definition: a solid-state drive ssd is a high-speed non-volatile storage device that uses nand not-and flash memory instead of mechanical platters resulting in faster load times and better durability
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Firmware corruption, sudden drop in write performance, or failure to communicate with the OS after a sudden power loss.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Update the drive’s firmware via the manufacturer’s software, check the BIOS to ensure the SATA mode is set to AHCI (Advanced Host Controller Interface), and ensure the OS is using native NVMe drivers if applicable.

definition: a basic sanitization method that writes a zero value to every block on a hard drive effectively erasing all previous data
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data remains "recoverable" if the drive is analyzed with advanced forensic tools, as a single pass of zeros may not meet high-security standards.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use a disk-wiping tool (like “diskpart” with the “clean all” command) to write zeros across the entire disk; for high-security environments, verify that this is the approved method for the data’s classification level.

definition: a troubleshooting technique that discharges residual electricity from hardware components forcing a complete power cycle of a device or motherboard
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A system will not power on, is stuck in a boot loop, or behaves erratically as if it has a configuration glitch.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Turn off the device, unplug the power source, remove the battery (if applicable), press and hold the power button for at least 30 seconds, reconnect the power, and attempt to turn the system on again.

definition: a physical hardware device like a key fob or smart card that generates an authentication code otp one-time password used as a second factor in multi-factor authentication mfa
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The user is unable to log in because the token is broken, the battery is dead, or the generated code is consistently rejected.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the time synchronization on the device (if applicable), check for a low battery indicator, and if the token is permanently faulty, use the administrative management console to revoke the old token and register a replacement.

definition: software licenses that require payment and govern the usage distribution and installation of proprietary software on hardware assets
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Software displays "Licensing Error" or "Trial Expired," or auditing tools flag the organization for unauthorized software usage.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the organization’s asset management database to verify license counts, install the correct license key, and ensure that the software installation conforms to the terms specified by the software vendor.

definition: digital rights management drm is a set of access control technologies used by hardware and software publishers to restrict the use of proprietary software and multimedia content
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Inability to play media on unauthorized devices or failures when attempting to install software across multiple systems.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the device has an active internet connection to verify DRM tokens, log into the correct account associated with the purchase, and check for compatibility issues between the content and the device's DRM implementation.

definition: the end-user license agreement eula is a legal contract between the software developer and the user detailing the terms and conditions under which the software may be used
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users violating software usage policies, such as installing a single-user license on multiple machines.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Review the EULA terms during software installation; if in doubt, consult the organizational legal or IT policy documentation regarding acceptable use.

definition: software licensing models that allow the source code to be inspected modified and enhanced by anyone often free of charge e g gpl general public license
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Misunderstanding regarding the freedom of the license, leading to accidental proprietary changes to open-source components.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Review the specific open-source license documentation (e.g., MIT, GPL, Apache) to understand attribution requirements and redistribution rights before modifying or including the code in proprietary projects.

definition: the administrative task of tracking hardware and software licenses to ensure the organization stays compliant with all vendor agreements
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Over-licensing (wasting money) or under-licensing (legal/compliance risk).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Implement an ITAM (IT Asset Management) system to centralize license keys, expiration dates, and deployment counts; conduct periodic audits to align inventory with active subscriptions.

definition: distinctions in licensing models where personal licenses are restricted to individual users while enterprise licenses allow for volume deployment and centralized management
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Attempting to use a personal license in an enterprise environment, leading to license rejection or compliance failure.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the license type during procurement and deployment; if an enterprise setup is required, ensure the software is activated using a volume license key or a management server.

definition: physical security devices that store cryptographic keys or generate authentication tokens to prove a user's identity when accessing a system
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unauthorized access if a token is stolen, or account lockouts due to lost tokens.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Implement a procedure for reporting lost tokens, enforce the use of PINs (Personal Identification Numbers) to unlock the token, and ensure the server-side authentication system tracks the token status.

definition: a mathematical algorithm that transforms an input of any size into a fixed-length string of characters used to verify data integrity e g sha secure hash algorithm or md5 message digest 5
ERROR SYMPTOMS: File checksum mismatch errors during software downloads or system corruption.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Compare the hash of the downloaded file with the official hash provided by the developer; if they do not match, the file is corrupt or has been tampered with, and should be re-downloaded.

definition: the time delay that occurs while the mechanical head of a hard drive seeks the correct track and rotates to the specific sector where the data is stored
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Slow disk read/write performance compared to SSDs.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Latency is an inherent physical property of HDDs; to improve performance, upgrade to an SSD, as mechanical drives cannot be "fixed" to lower latency beyond their rotational speed limit.

definition: the speed at which the internal platters of an hdd spin typically measured in rpm revolutions per minute which directly impacts read write latency and data transfer rates
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Slower-than-expected data access times if the drive is a low-RPM model (e.g., 5400 RPM).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the RPM rating on the drive label; for high-performance requirements, ensure the drive is rated at 7200 RPM or higher, or migrate the high-demand data to an SSD.

definition: a proprietary audio video interface used to transmit uncompressed video data and compressed or uncompressed digital audio data from an hdmi-compliant source device to a compatible computer monitor video projector or digital television tv
ERROR SYMPTOMS: No image displayed on the monitor, flickering screen, visual artifacts (static or lines), or audio not playing through the HDMI-connected speakers.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Inspect the cable for physical damage, ensure the cable is firmly seated in both the source and display ports, test with a different “known-good” cable, and verify the display settings in the OS (Operating System) to ensure the HDMI port is selected as the active output.

definition: a passive thermal management component typically made of aluminum or copper designed to increase the surface area of a heat-generating component such as a cpu central processing unit or gpu graphics processing unit to dissipate heat efficiently into the surrounding air
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Sudden system shutdowns during intensive tasks, excessive fan noise, or the system freezing after reaching high temperatures.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Clean dust buildup from the cooling fins using compressed air, re-apply thermal paste between the CPU and heat sink, and ensure the heat sink is mounted securely and making full contact with the integrated heat spreader.

definition: the diagnostic process of addressing thermal instability within a computing system by monitoring temperatures and ensuring that internal air circulation is adequate
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System restarts without warning, “Thermal Trip” errors in the BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) or UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) logs, or components failing prematurely.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Monitor system temperatures using software tools like “HWMonitor”, ensure all case fans are spinning in the correct direction, verify that air intake vents are not blocked, and clean any accumulated debris from inside the chassis.

definition: proper physical safety protocol for lifting heavy equipment such as servers or ups uninterruptible power supply units to prevent musculoskeletal injuries
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Back strain, neck pain, or accidental drops causing damage to equipment or physical injury to the technician.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Always lift with your legs, keeping the back straight and the object close to your body; if an object is too heavy for one person, seek assistance or use a mechanical lifting aid (like a dolly or server lift) to move the item.

definition: a centralized software application used by it support teams to log track manage and prioritize user-reported issues tickets throughout their lifecycle until resolution
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Inconsistent resolution times, lost communication regarding support requests, or difficulty tracking historical issue trends.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Review the ticket status in the application, ensure all relevant user information and troubleshooting steps taken so far are logged, and follow up with the user if the status has remained stagnant for too long.

definition: embedded documentation or linked resources provided by software vendors to assist users in understanding how to operate a program or troubleshoot common issues
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users unable to find information about specific application functions or an inability to access the local help database.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Press “F1” while the application is active to trigger the help context, check the “Help” menu within the application, or search the manufacturer’s website for an online version of the manual.

definition: a type of mechanical air filter that meets specific efficiency standards by removing at least 99 97 of dust pollen mold bacteria and any airborne particles with a size of 0 3 microns
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Reduced airflow in sensitive server environments or increased particulate accumulation in clean-room hardware.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the filter maintenance schedule, replace the filter if it appears clogged or dirty, and ensure that the replacement filter meets the required HEPA standards for the specific hardware or facility.

definition: a power-saving state in windows that saves all open documents and programs to the hard drive in a file called hiberfil sys and then powers down the computer completely allowing for a faster resume than a cold boot
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System fails to wake from hibernate, or there is insufficient disk space on the system drive to create the hibernation file.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Run the command “powercfg /hibernate on” in an elevated command prompt to ensure the feature is enabled, and check for adequate free disk space on the primary partition.

definition: addressing the delay between a command being sent over a network and the response being received often causing lag in real-time applications
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Stuttering audio/video in calls, slow web page responsiveness, or remote desktop sessions that feel unresponsive to user input.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the command “ping -t [destination IP]” to check for packet loss and jitter, check for background network usage (e.g., large downloads), and verify physical network cable integrity or switch port performance.

definition: features within an os or application that track file access or modifications allowing users to view logs of what changed or recover previous iterations of a document e g windows file history
ERROR SYMPTOMS: User cannot recover a previous version of a file after accidental deletion or overwriting.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Navigate to “Settings > Update & Security > Backup”, check if “File History” was enabled, and use the “Restore personal files” option to retrieve the desired file iteration.

definition: a logical group of keys subkeys and values in the windows registry that represents a portion of the system configuration e g hkey local machine or hkey current user
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System fails to boot, configuration settings are lost after a restart, or “Registry Corruption” errors appear during OS operation.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the “System File Checker” (“sfc /scannow”) to repair system files, or boot into the “Recovery Environment” and use the “System Restore” feature to roll back to a previously working registry backup.

definition: a specific directory on a network server or local machine designated for a user's personal documents desktop files and application settings
ERROR SYMPTOMS: User logs in but cannot save files, or cannot see their saved documents (often due to incorrect path mapping).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Active Directory Users and Computers” (in a domain environment) to verify the path in the user’s “Profile” tab, or check the folder permissions to ensure the user has “Modify” rights to their home directory.

definition: a virtualization manager that runs as an application on top of an existing host operating system e g vmware workstation or virtualbox sharing hardware resources managed by that host os
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Virtual machines (VMs) are extremely slow to load or experience severe graphical lag.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the host has enough RAM and CPU cores to support the VM, verify that “Hardware Virtualization” (VT-x or AMD-V) is enabled in the BIOS, and update the hypervisor software.

definition: a command-line utility used to display or set the current host name of the computer or network device
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A system is not showing the correct name on the network, or a script fails because it cannot resolve the computer’s identity.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the command prompt and type “hostname” to verify the current name; use the command “hostname [new_name]” (requires administrative privileges) to change it, or modify the system settings in the Control Panel.

definition: any device connected to a network that provides or consumes services ranging from personal computers to internet-enabled appliances
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Device is unreachable via the network, or it exhibits unexpected behavior that impacts other nodes.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the “ipconfig” (Windows) or “ifconfig” (Linux) command to verify local IP settings, check the status of the local firewall, and use the “ping” command to test connectivity to other network hosts.

definition: computing systems with dedicated functions often with real-time computing constraints embedded as part of a complete device such as those found in medical equipment or industrial controllers
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Device becomes unresponsive, requires frequent reboots, or crashes when performing specific functions.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Perform a power cycle, check for firmware updates from the manufacturer, and isolate the device from the network to determine if the issue is a software hang or a network-related communication error.

definition: a network of physical objects things embedded with sensors software and connectivity allowing them to exchange data with other devices and systems over the internet
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Smart home devices fail to communicate with the central hub, or firmware update failures lead to device bricking.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the wireless signal strength at the device location, verify the device is connected to the correct network segment (e.g., a guest or IoT-specific VLAN), and perform a factory reset if the device fails to authenticate.

definition: the distribution of network or application traffic across a number of servers to ensure no single server becomes overwhelmed improving reliability and responsiveness
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users experience slow response times from specific servers, or total service failure if one server in the cluster goes down and the load balancer doesn't redirect traffic.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the health check configuration in the load balancer settings, ensure all back-end servers are reachable, and check logs to see if traffic is correctly routing to active nodes.

definition: the practice of protecting networked devices and the data they transmit from unauthorized access or malicious attacks
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unusual network traffic spikes, unauthorized file access, or system alerts regarding malware infection.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Update OS and application security patches, enable and configure a host-based firewall, use strong authentication (MFA—Multi-Factor Authentication), and perform regular malware/vulnerability scans.

definition: a powerful computer or computer program that provides services resources or functionality to other programs or devices known as clients
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Clients cannot access shared files, databases, or web services hosted on the server.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the server is powered on, check if necessary services (e.g., DNS, DHCP, HTTP) are running in the “Services” console, and inspect the Event Viewer for application or system error codes.

definition: the protocol for handling components that generate significant heat e g cpus server chassis components to avoid thermal burns and protect sensitive hardware
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Minor burns to the technician or accidental damage to a component due to dropping it while trying to manage the heat.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Allow the system to cool down after shutdown for at least 15–20 minutes before touching internal components; if hardware must be handled while warm, use insulated gloves or handles.

definition: the ability to connect a device like a laptop to a docking station or peripheral while the computer is turned on and running without requiring a reboot
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The laptop does not recognize external monitors or peripherals after being placed in the dock.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the docking station firmware is updated, re-seat the connection, and check the “Device Manager” for any warnings regarding the docking hardware drivers.

definition: physical locations or devices like a smartphone that provide internet access to mobile devices over a wireless local area network wlan using a router connected to an internet service provider isp
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Devices can see the hotspot but cannot connect, or the internet connection is extremely slow.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the hotspot’s cellular signal strength, restart the hotspot device, ensure the security password is correct, and check if any bandwidth limits (data caps) have been reached.

definition: a dedicated physical device used to safeguard and manage digital keys perform encryption and support the secure boot process which ensures that only cryptographically signed code can execute during the boot process
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System refuses to boot, reporting “Invalid Signature” or “Secure Boot Violation.”
TROUBLESHOOTING: Enter the BIOS/UEFI, verify that the boot order and “Secure Boot” keys are correctly configured, and ensure that all installed hardware and drivers are signed by the manufacturer.

definition: an application-layer protocol used for transmitting hypermedia documents such as html hypertext markup language over the web it is the foundation of data communication for the world wide web
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Web pages fail to load or display “404 Not Found” or “500 Internal Server Error” messages.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify that the web server is running, check the network connection, and ensure that the URL is typed correctly; if testing locally, use a browser tool to inspect the server response headers.

definition: an extension of http that uses tls transport layer security or the older ssl secure sockets layer to encrypt the communication channel between a web browser and a server
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Browser displays “Your connection is not private” or “Certificate Invalid” warnings.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the date and time on the local computer (as this affects certificate validation), check if the website’s SSL certificate has expired, and ensure the certificate is issued by a trusted CA (Certificate Authority).

definition: a network layout where all nodes are connected to a central hub switch or concentrator
ERROR SYMPTOMS: If the central hub/switch fails, the entire network (or the branch connected to it) goes down.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the status lights on the central hub/switch; if off or blinking red, replace the unit; if the unit is functional, check the individual cabling running to the "spoke" nodes.

definition: a legacy networking device that connects multiple devices in a network segment and broadcasts all incoming data to every other port causing high traffic and collisions
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Extremely slow network performance or intermittent connection drops due to packet collisions.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Replace the hub with a network switch, which intelligently routes traffic to the destination rather than broadcasting it to every node.

definition: environmental settings managed in server rooms or data centers to ensure hardware operates within manufacturer-specified parameters e g preventing condensation or overheating
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Equipment corrosion (if too humid) or hardware failure (if too hot).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use environmental monitoring sensors to track data, adjust HVAC (Heating, Ventilation, Air Conditioning) systems accordingly, and ensure fans/ventilation are clear of obstructions.

definition: the technology of indoor and vehicular environmental comfort critical in data centers to maintain stable temperatures and humidity levels for server longevity
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data center temperature spikes leading to equipment shutdown.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Contact facility management, check HVAC unit error codes, and use portable cooling units as a temporary measure if the primary climate control fails.

definition: a computing environment that combines a public cloud e g aws amazon web services and a private cloud e g on-premises servers allowing data and applications to be shared between them
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data synchronization failures between on-premises storage and the public cloud, or service connectivity issues.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the VPN (Virtual Private Network) or direct connection tunnel is active, check cloud provider status dashboards, and ensure local firewall rules allow traffic to the cloud service.

definition: a storage device that combines traditional spinning magnetic platters hdd with a small amount of high-speed flash memory ssd to act as a cache speeding up frequently accessed files
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Drive performance degrades over time, or the system experiences long delays when opening applications that aren't in the flash cache.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the drive firmware is updated, run drive diagnostic software to check both the mechanical and flash components, and consider replacing the drive with a full SSD if performance requirements increase.

definition: software or hardware that creates and runs virtual machines by abstracting the physical hardware into independent virtual environments
ERROR SYMPTOMS: VMs fail to start, or host system performance drops significantly when a VM is running.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify BIOS/UEFI virtualization settings, allocate sufficient RAM and CPU to the VMs, and check for hypervisor software updates.

definition: a native hypervisor developed by microsoft that allows for the creation of virtual machines on x86-64 systems running windows
ERROR SYMPTOMS: VMs fail to launch, or network communication between the VM and the physical network is blocked.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the “Hyper-V Manager” for VM status, ensure the “Virtual Switch” is correctly configured, and check if the “Hyper-V” feature is properly enabled in “Windows Features.”

definition: a type 2 hypervisor developed by oracle that allows users to run different operating systems as virtual machines on a single host
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Guest OS fails to boot, or “Guest Additions” are not functioning correctly.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Reinstall “Guest Additions” within the VM, ensure the host meets memory requirements, and check “Settings” for the correct virtualization mode.

definition: a powerful type 2 hypervisor that allows for the creation and management of complex virtual networking environments and vms on windows or linux hosts
ERROR SYMPTOMS: VM performance lag, or inability to connect the VM to the internet (NAT—Network Address Translation vs. Bridged mode issues).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Review the “Virtual Network Editor” settings, ensure the “VMware Tools” package is updated, and check for conflicts with other virtualization software installed on the same host.

definition: a cloud computing model that delivers virtualized computing resources such as virtual servers network storage and load balancers over the internet allowing organizations to rent infrastructure rather than purchasing physical hardware
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Connectivity loss to the virtual data center, inability to scale resources (CPU/RAM) as defined in the service level agreement (SLA), or failure of cloud-based virtual machines (VMs) to boot.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify internet connectivity to the cloud provider, check the cloud management console for system health alerts or resource exhaustion, and review firewall configurations or security groups for misconfigured access rules.

definition: the standards organization that oversees global ip internet protocol address allocation autonomous system number allocation root zone management in the dns domain name system and other ip-related symbols and numbers
ERROR SYMPTOMS: N/A (This is a regulatory body, not a hardware component).
TROUBLESHOOTING: If network services are failing due to IP allocation issues, verify that local DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) servers are configured correctly and not conflicting with IANA-reserved private address ranges.

definition: apple s proprietary cloud storage and computing service that synchronizes data including photos files and device backups across ios iphone os ipados and macos devices
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Files not syncing across devices, storage full warnings, or failure to perform device backups.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the device is signed into the correct Apple ID, check the internet connection, verify that “iCloud Drive” is enabled in “Settings”, and check if the storage quota has been exceeded.

definition: small graphical representations of files folders applications or shortcuts that allow users to launch programs or access data quickly within the windows graphical user interface
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Icons are missing, become generic white squares, or fail to respond when double-clicked.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Right-click the desktop and ensure “Show desktop icons” is checked in the “View” menu, or rebuild the icon cache by deleting the “IconCache.db” file in the user’s local “AppData” folder and restarting the system.

definition: a legacy interface standard also known as pata parallel advanced technology attachment used to connect storage devices like hard drives and optical drives to the motherboard using wide 40-pin ribbon cables
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Drive not detected during BIOS POST (Power-On Self-Test), “Disk read error” messages, or physical signs of cable wear/damage causing intermittent connectivity.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the IDE cable is securely connected to both the drive and the motherboard, verify the “Master/Slave” jumper settings on the back of the drive are correct, and replace the ribbon cable with a known-good one.

definition: the initial phase of the standardized troubleshooting methodology where a technician gathers information observes symptoms and questions the user to pinpoint the cause of a system issue
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Ineffective repair attempts, wasted time, or misdiagnosis of the root cause due to lack of information.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Question the user about recent changes (software/hardware), identify the scope of the problem (is it one user or many?), and review system logs to verify the reported symptoms before attempting any physical or software-based repairs.

definition: a security tool that monitors network traffic or system activity for suspicious patterns or policy violations and alerts administrators to potential security breaches
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Sudden network performance degradation (if the IDS is overburdened), or “False Positives” flagging legitimate traffic as malicious.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Review the IDS log files, tune the detection rules to reduce noise, and ensure that the IDS signatures are up to date to properly identify modern threat vectors.

word: IEEE (Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers), PoE standards
definition: the professional organization that defines standards for networking including ieee 802 3af at bt for poe power over ethernet which allows electrical power to be transmitted over twisted-pair ethernet cabling
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Powered devices (e.g., VoIP—Voice over IP phones, IP cameras) fail to turn on or reboot frequently.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the switch port is PoE-enabled, check if the total power budget of the switch has been exceeded, and test with a residential length Ethernet cable to rule out power loss over long distances.

definition: a fundamental programming or scripting construct that executes a specific block of code only if a specified condition is evaluated as true
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Scripts fail to run, behave unpredictably, or execute the wrong code block, often indicating a logical error in the condition evaluation.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use a debugger or add “print” statements to output the values of variables before they are evaluated by the “if” statement to ensure the logic matches the intended workflow.

definition: a deployment method where a standardized master installation of an os applications and settings is captured into an image file e g wim windows imaging format and distributed to multiple computers to ensure consistent configuration
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Systems fail to boot after imaging, drivers are missing for specific hardware models, or the image fails to deploy due to network interruptions.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the image source integrity, ensure the deployment server (e.g., WDS—Windows Deployment Services) is reachable, and check that the correct mass storage drivers are injected into the image for the target hardware.

definition: the use of windows re windows recovery environment to restore a system to a previously captured state or a factory default image following a catastrophic system failure or data corruption
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The operating system will not boot (e.g., "Inaccessible Boot Device" BSOD—Blue Screen of Death).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Boot into Windows RE by interrupting the startup process three times, select “Troubleshoot > Advanced Options”, and use “System Image Recovery” to point the system to the backup location of the image file.

definition: an email protocol that allows users to access and manage email messages on a server synchronizing the folder state across multiple devices
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Emails are not syncing between devices, or “Connection Timed Out” errors occur when checking for new mail.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the server settings (port 143 for non-SSL, 993 for SSL/TLS), check the network connection, and ensure the username and password are correctly entered.

definition: a unique 15-digit number used to identify individual gsm global system for mobile communications and umts universal mobile telecommunications system mobile devices on a cellular network
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Device is denied access to cellular service, or the carrier cannot locate or identify the specific handset.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Type “*#06#” on the dial pad to display the IMEI; if the device is blocked or “blacklisted,” contact the cellular provider to verify its status.

definition: the assessment of how resource-heavy applications cpu ram disk network affect the stability and performance of a workstation or mobile device
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System sluggishness, high fan speed, or frequent crashes when launching specific software.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use “Task Manager” (Windows) or “Activity Monitor” (macOS) to identify high resource-consuming processes, uninstall unnecessary background applications, or upgrade hardware components (like RAM) to meet application requirements.

definition: a category of printers that generate images by physically striking an inked ribbon against paper commonly used for multi-part forms and receipt printing
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Faded print, broken pins (in dot-matrix), or mechanical jams preventing the print head from moving.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the ink ribbon for dryness or damage, clean the print head with isopropyl alcohol, and inspect the tractor-feed mechanism for paper alignment issues.

definition: the internal parts of an impact printer including the print head ribbon cartridge tractor-feed gears and platen
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Uneven print quality or mechanical failure of one of these critical components.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Visually inspect each component for signs of wear, ensure the ribbon is properly tensioned, and verify that the platen is not damaged or grooved.

definition: an impact printer that uses a circular disk the daisy wheel with raised character forms at the ends of its spokes striking the ribbon one character at a time
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Missing characters in printed text, or the wheel failing to rotate to the correct character.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Clean the wheel surface to remove debris, and ensure the hammer mechanism is aligned correctly with the character spokes.

definition: an impact printer that uses a matrix of pins which strike an inked ribbon to form text and graphics on the page
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Horizontal white lines appearing across the printed output, indicating one or more pins in the print head are broken.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Replace the print head assembly if multiple pins are broken, or clean the head if it is simply jammed by dust and ink.

definition: periodic procedures required to keep impact printers functional including ribbon replacement paper alignment and cleaning of the print head and feed path
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Paper jams, ink smudging, or mechanical grinding sounds.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Vacuum out paper dust regularly, keep the carriage rods lightly lubricated, and replace the ribbon cartridge as soon as print quality begins to fade.

definition: a form of social engineering where an attacker pretends to be someone else such as a technician executive or customer to gain unauthorized access to information or systems
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unexpected requests for password resets, sensitive data, or physical entry into restricted areas from individuals claiming to be internal staff.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Always verify the identity of the requester through official channels, check the employee directory, and never provide credentials or sensitive data over the phone without following established verification policies.

definition: situations where a computer restarts or turns off unexpectedly without user input often caused by thermal issues power supply failure or os instability
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The PC powers off while in use or restarts during boot.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check system temperatures, test the PSU (Power Supply Unit) with a multimeter to ensure stable voltages, check for OS updates, and disable the "Automatically restart" feature in “System Properties” to capture the BSOD error code for analysis.

definition: a unique number stored on the sim subscriber identity module card that identifies a user on a cellular network
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The mobile device is unable to register on the cellular network (e.g., “No SIM card found”).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Remove and reseat the SIM card, ensure the card is not damaged, or contact the carrier to verify that the IMSI is correctly associated with an active subscription.

definition: formal documents created after a security or system incident to record exactly what happened what impact it had and what steps were taken to resolve it
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Future incidents go unresolved or escalate due to a lack of documentation of previous events.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure all incidents are logged in the organization’s ticketing or incident management system, document the timeline of events clearly, and conduct a post-incident review to update procedures.

definition: the organized approach to addressing and managing the aftermath of a security breach or cyberattack to limit damage and reduce recovery time
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System unavailability, data loss, or evidence of unauthorized access in system logs.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Follow the established incident response plan (IRP), starting with identification, followed by containment, eradication, and finally, recovery and lessons learned.

definition: the chronological documentation or paper trail that records the sequence of custody control transfer and analysis of evidence collected during an incident
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Evidence is ruled inadmissible in a legal or disciplinary hearing because it cannot be proven that it wasn't tampered with.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Maintain a strict log of who accessed the evidence, when, and for what purpose; keep all physical evidence in secured containers and digitally hash files to ensure integrity.

definition: the stages of an incident where the threat is isolated containment the root cause is removed eradication and systems are restored to a known good state recovery
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The threat persists after initial cleanup attempts.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Disconnect affected systems from the network, wipe and re-image the hardware, change all compromised credentials, and monitor traffic closely to ensure the attacker is gone.

definition: the process of determining whether an event is truly a security incident and identifying the scope of the potential damage
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Alerts from security tools or user reports of strange system behavior.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Analyze logs, correlate events from multiple sources (e.g., IDS, Firewall, Server logs), and use forensic tools to identify the nature and source of the threat.

definition: the recording of all actions taken during the incident response lifecycle to ensure compliance and assist in post-incident analysis
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Missing information regarding who authorized certain actions or why specific systems were taken offline.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Maintain a detailed incident log that records all findings, technical actions, and communications, ensuring it is timestamped and signed off by authorized personnel.

definition: the immediate actions taken by the first it staff member to arrive at the scene of an incident focused on preserving evidence and limiting initial impact
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Evidence is overwritten or critical information is lost due to an uncoordinated response.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Secure the area, take photos of physical equipment if necessary, prevent unnecessary system reboots (which clears RAM), and follow the predefined “First Responder” checklist.

definition: the systematic repeatable phases of an incident response process preparation detection analysis containment eradication recovery and post-incident activity
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Inconsistent or chaotic response to security events.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Regularly review and update the incident response lifecycle documentation, conduct tabletop exercises, and ensure all staff are trained on their roles.

definition: the proactive steps taken before an incident occurs such as policy development staff training and setting up logging monitoring infrastructure
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Lack of preparedness leading to slow reaction times during an actual attack.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure security policies are clearly defined, conduct regular backups, train staff on social engineering detection, and perform vulnerability assessments.

definition: a backup type that only copies files that have changed since the last backup whether it was a full or incremental backup providing efficient storage usage but potentially slower recovery times
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data recovery takes too long or fails because of missing incremental backup sets.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure all incremental backup sets are properly indexed; for faster recovery, use a combination of full weekly backups and daily incremental backups.

definition: a windows configuration tool that allows users to select which locations folders drives the system should index to provide faster file searching
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Windows Search is slow, or recently created files are not appearing in search results.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Indexing Options” in the Control Panel, click “Modify” to ensure the necessary folders are included, and if the index is corrupted, click “Advanced” and select “Rebuild”.

definition: log entries in the windows event viewer that track routine operations such as a service starting successfully or an application completing a standard task
ERROR SYMPTOMS: N/A (These are standard operating notifications, not errors).
TROUBLESHOOTING: If these are overwhelming the log file, use the “Filter” option in the Event Viewer to hide them, allowing you to focus on “Warning” or “Error” events.

definition: an authentication factor based on something you are such as biometric data e g fingerprint iris scan or facial recognition
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Biometric sensor failure or incorrect rejection of a valid user (false rejection).

definition: an infrastructure management framework within active directory that enables administrators to configure and enforce baseline operating system configurations security controls and desktop policies globally across all domain-joined computers and users

TROUBLESHOOTING: Open an elevated command shell prompt on the target host and execute the forcing update command tool "gpresult /h report.html" to generate a comprehensive Group Policy configuration diagnostic report, and run "gpupdate /force" to refresh policies.

definition: physical standalone hardware pieces such as usb smart keys or digital display key fobs that generate or hold cryptographic keys used during multifactor authentication procedures
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Token devices display blank screens, or authentication terminals fail to read attached physical smart keys.

definition: a dedicated secured filesystem directory path mapped on a local storage volume or corporate network file server that is assigned exclusively to an individual user account to store personal documents and configuration files
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users encounter permissions errors when saving personal files, or network home folders fail to mount during system login sequences.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the user account object configurations properties within Active Directory, check the profile paths mapping tabs to verify network paths are spelt correctly, and verify the user has explicit full-control permission flags over their directory folder.

definition: administrative command line files or shell script automation utilities that execute programmatically in the background immediately after a user successfully log into their network account automated to map shared drive network connections configure printers or check environment variables
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Workstations complete login sequences but lack required shared network drive map letters, or text terminal script execution errors pop up on screen.

definition: mobile device management mdm encompasses the centralized software server architectures used to enroll monitor configure patch track and secure mobile smartphones tablets and laptop form factors across an enterprise footprint
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Mobile endpoints bypass standard security baseline rules, install unapproved mobile apps, or fail to apply corporate Wi-Fi credentials.

definition: collection buckets inside directory services and operating systems used to compile multiple user accounts together under a unified security container identity to simplify permission management across shared network folders and assets

definition: short message service sms text messages used as an out-of-band delivery tool to transmit numeric verification pin tokens to a user's mobile device during step-up multi-factor authentication sequences
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Account verification loops time out because verification text messages fail to deliver to the user's mobile device, or login sessions fail due to delayed transit text arrivals.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify cellular carrier network signal metrics on the target phone, confirm the registered mobile phone number digits match the account identity grid field variables exactly, and recommend moving to software-based authentication applications to avoid SIM-swapping risks.

definition: software-based multi-factor authentication applications such as google authenticator or microsoft authenticator installed on a smartphone or computer to generate dynamic time-based one-time passwords totp that change every 30 seconds

TROUBLESHOOTING: Launch the smartphone authenticator app configuration menu screen, click the options toggle tool to run an internal time synchronization routine, ensure the smartphone's network time matches the global standard time, and re-attempt the login sequence.

definition: user account control uac is a windows security subsystem that prompts users for explicit confirmation or administrative credentials before allowing applications to make modifications to the system registry or operating system core files
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Malicious software packages install background drivers completely silently without any security warning alerts prompting across the active user desktop layout screen.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the Windows Control Panel interface box tool, search for and click into the "Change User Account Control settings" link item path, raise the selection slider control notch up to the baseline recommended option "Always notify", and commit changes to enforce approval prompts.

definition: the distinct operational user configuration data records and personal file space sets including background preferences system registry adjustments and document directories that the operating system loads when an individual account authenticates
