definition: software programs designed to detect quarantine and remove various forms of malicious software including viruses trojans worms and spyware from a system
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unexpected system reboots, browser redirects to suspicious sites, sluggish performance, or persistent pop-up advertisements.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the antimalware database is updated, perform a “Full Scan” in offline mode (if available), and check for suspicious background processes in the “Task Manager”.

definition: specialized security software that continuously monitors system activity for signatures or heuristic behaviors consistent with known computer viruses protecting the system from infection
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Virus definition updates failing, constant alerts regarding blocked access to system files, or high CPU (Central Processing Unit) usage by the antivirus service.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Reinstall the antivirus client, clear the cache, run the “Repair” function from the “Control Panel > Programs and Features”, and ensure compatibility with any active Windows Defender settings.

definition: a unified account used to access apple services e g icloud app store imessage which serves as a central point of identity security for apple devices
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The user is unable to sign into iCloud, device activation fails, or the account is locked due to multiple failed authentication attempts.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Navigate to “iforgot.apple.com” to reset the password, verify the account email address, and check if 2FA (Two-Factor Authentication) is preventing access on new devices.

definition: the application layer of security involving the hardening of software to prevent vulnerabilities like sql structured query language injection buffer overflows and unauthorized execution
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Software crashing frequently, showing memory errors, or exhibiting unexpected behavior that suggests an integrity compromise.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify application version compatibility, check for software patches or updates, and ensure the application is running within a restricted user account context.

definition: software tools that generate time-based one-time passwords totp to provide mfa multi-factor authentication adding a layer of security beyond just a username and password
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The user is unable to log into a service because the generated codes are rejected or the application fails to sync with the server.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the system time on the device is synchronized with the network time (NTP - Network Time Protocol), as time-drift will invalidate TOTP codes; verify settings in the authenticator app.

definition: an authentication method that identifies users based on unique physiological or behavioral traits such as fingerprints facial structure or retinal patterns
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The sensor fails to detect the user, errors occur during the scanning process, or the OS fails to associate the biometric scan with the user account.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Clean the biometric sensor (e.g., fingerprint reader), ensure the driver is current in “Device Manager”, and re-register the biometric data in the “Sign-in options” menu.

definition: the low-level software initialized during the boot process bios - basic input output system that provides foundational security controls such as boot password protection
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The system is bypassed by unauthorized boot media, or critical settings are altered without administrative authorization.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Enter the BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) setup by pressing the designated key during startup, set a supervisor password, and configure the boot order to disable booting from removable media.

definition: a windows feature that provides full-volume encryption to protect data at rest by encrypting the entire drive including the os operating system partition
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The system refuses to boot, or the user is prompted for a BitLocker recovery key that they do not have.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Locate the recovery key in the user’s Microsoft account or AD (Active Directory) backup, or use the command “manage-bde -status” to check the encryption volume health.

definition: the configuration and security management of web browsers to prevent malicious web-based attacks like cross-site scripting xss and drive-by downloads
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Pop-ups occurring constantly, homepage changing automatically, or browser performance degradation due to malicious extensions.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Clear the browser cache and cookies, disable suspicious extensions in the browser settings, and reset the browser to default configuration if issues persist.

word: Security: BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) policies
definition: an administrative set of rules governing the use of personal mobile devices e g smartphones laptops for corporate work focusing on mdm mobile device management and data containerization
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Corporate data is leaked to personal applications, or an employee device is lost without the ability to remotely wipe company data.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Enforce device enrollment in the company MDM (Mobile Device Management) solution, ensure full-disk encryption is active, and configure remote wipe capabilities.

definition: physical security devices e g kensington locks used to tether workstations or monitors to a desk preventing theft of hardware
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The lock mechanism is damaged, the key is lost, or the tether point on the computer chassis is broken.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Inspect the slot for debris, apply lubricant if the locking mechanism is stiff, or replace the entire physical cable lock assembly.

definition: the management of network-based security ensuring that remote or local connections are authenticated encrypted and isolated according to organizational security policy
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unexpected connection timeouts, inability to access secure resources (e.g., VPN - Virtual Private Network), or certificate warnings during connection attempts.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the VPN (Virtual Private Network) configuration, check that firewall ports are open, and ensure root certificates are correctly installed on the client machine.

definition: the protection of sensitive information through encryption access control lists acls and data loss prevention dlp strategies
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data being accessed by unauthorized users, or files showing signs of corruption or tampering.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Review NTFS (New Technology File System) permissions, verify that encryption is active on the folder, and audit file access logs.

word: Security: DNSSEC (Domain Name System Security Extensions)
definition: a suite of extensions that adds security to dns domain name system by providing origin authentication and data integrity through digital signatures
ERROR SYMPTOMS: DNS (Domain Name System) resolution failures, or websites failing to load due to a mismatch in cryptographic signatures.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the command “nslookup -debug” or “dig +dnssec” to diagnose resolution issues and check the chain of trust in the DNS (Domain Name System) records.

definition: the implementation of security controls for email including encryption s mime - secure multipurpose internet mail extensions spam filtering and phishing awareness
ERROR SYMPTOMS: High volume of spam, emails being flagged by security filters, or sensitive data being sent over unencrypted channels.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Update email client filtering rules, ensure TLS (Transport Layer Security) is configured for outgoing/incoming mail, and educate users on identifying phishing attempts.

definition: the process of encoding information so that only authorized parties can read it using cryptographic algorithms to ensure confidentiality
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data unreadable to the end user, or performance degradation during intensive I/O (Input/Output) operations on encrypted volumes.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the status of the encryption key, check if the system service (e.g., BitLocker service) is running, and re-attempt decryption or key recovery if necessary.

definition: a biometric security measure that identifies individuals by comparing facial geometry against stored biometric data
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The device fails to recognize the user under different lighting conditions, or the recognition engine is consistently inaccurate.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Improve lighting, re-register the facial profile in “Settings”, and ensure the camera lens is clean.

definition: administrative controls that determine which users or groups can read write or execute files and folders within an os operating system filesystem
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users being unable to open files they should have access to, or sensitive files being readable by unauthorized users.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Right-click the file or folder, select “Properties”, go to the “Security” tab, and review the ACLs (Access Control Lists) to verify permissions.

definition: the implementation of encryption at the filesystem level ensuring that files stored on the disk cannot be read without the correct decryption key
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Files showing up as encrypted (e.g., green text in Windows) but being inaccessible to the user.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the user account’s EFS (Encrypting File System) certificate status and recover the file using a backup certificate if possible.

definition: the management and security of individual files to prevent unauthorized modification or accidental deletion
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Files being modified unexpectedly or disappearing from shared folders.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Audit file usage logs, verify user permissions, and restore the file from the last known good backup.

definition: a biometric method that captures the ridges and valleys of a finger to verify identity
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Fingerprint reader not responding, or consistently failing to match the user's print.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Clean the reader surface, ensure the user's hands are clean, and re-enroll the fingerprint in the OS (Operating System) settings.

definition: hardware or software appliances that monitor and filter incoming and outgoing network traffic based on an organization's security rules
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Legitimate traffic being blocked, applications failing to connect to the internet, or the firewall service failing to start.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the firewall rules configuration, ensure the necessary ports are open (e.g., 80, 443), and inspect logs for blocked traffic entries.

definition: controls applied to directory structures that define which users can access the contents or modify the contents of a folder
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users unable to list files inside a directory or access sub-folders.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check for permission inheritance settings on the parent folder, and modify the “Advanced” security settings to correct inheritance issues.

definition: a logical collection of user accounts used to simplify administration and apply security permissions to multiple users at once
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A user is unable to access resources they should have access to based on their role.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the user account is a member of the correct security group in “Active Directory Users and Computers” and verify group-based access policies.

definition: an isolated network segment typically provided via a wi-fi access point that provides internet access to visitors without allowing access to the internal corporate network
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Guests can access internal resources, or the guest network is inaccessible.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the guest network is on a separate VLAN (Virtual Local Area Network) and verify that the firewall is correctly blocking access from the guest VLAN to the internal network.

word: Security: HSM (Hardware Security Module), Secure Boot
definition: a specialized physical computing device that safeguards and manages digital keys often used in conjunction with secure boot to ensure only signed firmware runs
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Boot process fails due to invalid key signatures in the HSM (Hardware Security Module).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the integrity of the key storage on the HSM (Hardware Security Module) and ensure the firmware signatures are current.

definition: a monitoring system that detects suspicious activity and potential security threats on a network alerting administrators without blocking the traffic itself
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Excessive false positive alerts, or the system missing genuine malicious activity.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Tune the IDS (Intrusion Detection System) rule set, update the attack signature database, and verify the network connectivity between the monitoring port and the IDS (Intrusion Detection System).

definition: the security of interconnected devices e g smart thermostats cameras which often lack robust security features making them targets for botnets
ERROR SYMPTOMS: IoT (Internet of Things) devices acting strangely, being used in DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) attacks, or showing unauthorized remote management access.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Isolate IoT (Internet of Things) devices on a separate VLAN (Virtual Local Area Network), change default passwords, and ensure firmware is updated to the latest version.

definition: a proactive security technology that not only detects suspicious network activity but also automatically blocks the malicious traffic
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Legitimate traffic being dropped, or the IPS (Intrusion Prevention System) becoming a network bottleneck.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Review the IPS (Intrusion Prevention System) policies to ensure legitimate services are whitelisted, and verify hardware performance to ensure it can handle current traffic loads.

definition: security solutions like clamav configured for linux-based systems to scan for malicious files and email threats
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Malicious scripts executing on Linux systems or unauthorized file modification.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the command “freshclam” to update definitions, run the scan from the terminal, and check system logs for detection events.

definition: a set of software-based controls e g firewalls acls encryption designed to limit access to computer resources networks and data ensuring that only authenticated users can perform authorized tasks
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unauthorized access to restricted network shares, unexpected elevation of user privileges, or audit logs showing failed access attempts to system-level configuration files.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Review the “Local Group Policy” and “Active Directory” permission sets, ensure MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication) is enforced, and run the command “gpresult /r” to verify effective security policies on a workstation.

definition: any program or file that is intentionally harmful to a computer network or server including viruses worms trojan horses ransomware and spyware
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System performance degradation, mysterious file deletion or modification, browser homepage redirects, and excessive pop-up ads during normal operation.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Disconnect the infected machine from the network, run a full scan using updated antimalware software, check for malicious items in “Startup” via “Task Manager”, and use “Malwarebytes” or similar tools to remove rootkits.

definition: security protocols and configurations applied to portable devices e g smartphones tablets to protect corporate data often managed through mdm mobile device management platforms
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data breach on a mobile device, inability to connect to corporate Wi-Fi due to certificate issues, or a device being lost without remote-wipe protection.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Enroll the device in the organization’s MDM (Mobile Device Management) solution, verify that full-disk encryption is active, and enforce biometric or strong passcode requirements.

definition: a set of communication protocols that enables two electronic devices to establish communication by bringing them within close proximity typically 4 cm or less often used for contactless payments and authentication
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Contactless payment failure, or NFC (Near Field Communication) tag readers failing to initiate a connection when the device is placed in proximity.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the NFC (Near Field Communication) feature is enabled in the device “Settings”, remove any thick metal cases that may block the signal, and restart the device to reset the radio hardware.

definition: a string of characters used for authenticating a user identity serving as the primary credential for accessing local and network resources
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Account lockout due to excessive failed attempts, or suspected compromise due to password reuse across multiple services.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Reset the password via the administrative account, enforce complex password requirements (minimum length, mixed character types) in “Group Policy”, and implement MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication).

definition: the collective security posture of a personal computer including hardware e g chassis locks firmware e g bios uefi passwords and os operating system security
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unauthorized access to system hardware, or repeated attempts to compromise the workstation locally.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Set a BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) administrator password, enable full-disk encryption, and use physical security measures like Kensington locks to secure the hardware.

word: Security: PCI-DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard)
definition: a set of security standards designed to ensure that all companies that accept process store or transmit credit card information maintain a secure environment
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Failure to pass a quarterly network security audit, or data exposure resulting in non-compliance fines.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Review the internal network against PCI-DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) requirements, ensure network segmentation is in place, and perform regular vulnerability scanning using authorized tools.

definition: rules assigned to users or groups that dictate their level of access read write execute modify to files folders or network resources
ERROR SYMPTOMS: User “Access Denied” errors when trying to open files or folders, or unauthorized users being able to modify sensitive corporate documents.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Right-click the object, go to “Properties > Security”, and verify the ACL (Access Control List) entries; ensure permissions follow the “Principle of Least Privilege”.

definition: the protection of personnel hardware networks and data from physical actions and events that could cause serious loss or damage such as theft fire or vandalism
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unauthorized physical access to the server room, missing peripherals, or hardware tampering.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Install CCTV (Closed-Circuit Television) cameras, use badge-access readers for restricted areas, and ensure all hardware is secured in locked racks or enclosures.

definition: a numerical code used to verify the identity of a user often used as a secondary or local authentication factor in windows hello or on mobile devices
ERROR SYMPTOMS: PIN (Personal Identification Number) is rejected, or the biometric sensor fails, requiring PIN (Personal Identification Number) fallback which also fails.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the “I forgot my PIN” link on the login screen to reset credentials using the primary account password, and ensure the TPM (Trusted Platform Module) chip is functioning correctly.

definition: browser settings that prevent automated unwanted windows pop-ups from opening which are often used for advertising or malicious delivery
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Browser becomes sluggish due to too many pop-up ads, or users are redirected to phishing sites by clicking on intrusive pop-ups.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Navigate to browser “Settings > Privacy and security > Site Settings”, and ensure “Pop-ups and redirects” is set to “Don't allow”.

definition: the practice of physically disabling or blocking unused ports e g usb ethernet on a workstation or switch to prevent unauthorized peripheral connections or network access
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unauthorized USB (Universal Serial Bus) storage devices being used, or unauthorized network nodes connecting to a wall jack.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use physical port locks for USB (Universal Serial Bus) ports, or disable unused switch ports via the switch management CLI (Command Line Interface) using the command “shutdown”.

definition: security hardening of network-connected printers and mfds multifunction devices to prevent them from becoming entry points for network attacks
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unauthorized access to print logs, or the MFD (Multifunction Device) being used as a staging point for network scanning.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Change default administrative passwords, disable unused services (like Telnet or FTP - File Transfer Protocol), and enable disk encryption on MFD (Multifunction Device) internal storage.

definition: a file attribute that prevents users from modifying or deleting the content of a file serving as a basic integrity control
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users unable to save changes to a file, or receiving an “Access Denied” error when attempting to modify a document.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Right-click the file, select “Properties”, and uncheck the “Read-only” box in the “Attributes” section; if the file is on a network share, verify NTFS (New Technology File System) permissions.

definition: a feature that allows an authorized user to launch an application with higher-level privileges than their standard account normally possesses facilitating tasks like software installation
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Applications failing to run correctly due to insufficient permission levels.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Right-click the application executable and select “Run as administrator”, or use the command “runas /user:[administrator] [application.exe]” in the CMD (Command Prompt) window.

definition: the psychological manipulation of people into performing actions or divulging confidential information rather than using technical hacking techniques
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A user claims they were tricked into giving their password, or suspicious unauthorized personnel are seen asking for sensitive data.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Conduct security awareness training, implement strict verification policies for help-desk requests, and mandate reporting procedures for suspicious contacts.

definition: a networking environment designed for small businesses or home use which requires tailored security configurations to protect against external internet threats
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unauthorized devices appearing on the wireless network, or evidence of external intrusion attempts in the router logs.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Change default router login credentials, update firmware to the latest version, disable WPS (Wi-Fi Protected Setup), and configure a strong WPA3 (Wi-Fi Protected Access 3) password.

definition: a dedicated security appliance or cloud service that filters incoming and outgoing email to block spam phishing attempts and malware before it reaches the user s inbox
ERROR SYMPTOMS: An influx of spam emails reaching end users, or legitimate business emails being blocked as false positives.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Update the spam filter’s “Allow/Block” lists, adjust the heuristic scanning sensitivity, and verify the gateway’s DNS (Domain Name System) reputation configuration.

definition: an authentication method that allows a user to log in with a single id and password to gain access to a connected system or multiple software applications
ERROR SYMPTOMS: User cannot access any associated applications, or one failure point causes a complete lockout across all platforms.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the status of the SSO (Single Sign-On) identity provider (e.g., Azure AD), check the user’s token expiration, and confirm proper synchronization between the directory service and the applications.

definition: a threat is a potential for loss or damage to a system while a vulnerability is a weakness in that system that can be exploited by a threat
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Systems being compromised, or security scanners reporting unpatched software flaws.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Conduct regular vulnerability assessments using tools like “Nessus”, prioritize patching critical flaws, and implement mitigation strategies (e.g., firewalls) where immediate patching is impossible.

definition: a cryptographic protocol designed to provide communication security over a computer network commonly used in web browsing and email
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Websites display “Insecure” warnings, or connections fail due to outdated or weak protocol versions (e.g., TLS 1.0/1.1 being deprecated).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Update the server configuration to support TLS 1.2 or 1.3, and ensure clients have the latest root CA (Certificate Authority) certificates installed.

definition: the windows interface used to manage os operating system updates security features like windows defender and recovery options
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System updates failing, or security features not active/showing errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Settings > Update & Security”, check for available updates, click “Troubleshoot” to run the “Windows Update Troubleshooter”, and ensure the “Windows Update” service is running.

definition: a digital identity representing an individual which controls their access privileges and settings within a computing environment
ERROR SYMPTOMS: User account compromised by malicious activity, or user unable to authenticate due to account lockout.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Reset account credentials, check “Active Directory” logs for signs of brute-force attempts, and verify that the account has not been added to unauthorized security groups.

definition: a logical grouping of user accounts that simplifies the management of permissions and security policies
ERROR SYMPTOMS: User has incorrect access permissions, or they are denied access to resources they require for their job role.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify group membership using “Active Directory Users and Computers” (for enterprise environments) or “Local Users and Groups” (for standalone machines).

definition: a security appliance that consolidates multiple security functions such as firewall antivirus ids ips intrusion detection prevention system and content filtering into a single device
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The UTM (Unified Threat Management) device becomes a network bottleneck, or it fails to filter traffic as configured due to a service error.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the device resource utilization, verify rule priorities in the UTM (Unified Threat Management) dashboard, and ensure all security engine signatures are current.

definition: the use of software to create virtual representations of servers storage or networks requiring specific security considerations to prevent 'vm escape' attacks
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unauthorized access to a virtual machine (VM), or a compromise in one VM affecting others on the same host.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Keep the hypervisor patched, implement strict network isolation (VLANs) between VMs, and use secure console access methods.

definition: the practice of verifying the security and authenticity of websites before entering sensitive information typically checked via https hypertext protocol secure and domain validation
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Phishing attempts masquerading as legitimate websites, or browser certificate error warnings.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Train users to inspect the URL for spelling errors, check the padlock icon for a valid certificate, and use bookmark-only access for sensitive sites.

definition: the built-in microsoft antivirus solution that provides real-time protection against malware and other threats
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Antivirus service disabled, or updates failing, leaving the system vulnerable.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Windows Security”, navigate to “Virus & threat protection”, and click “Quick scan”; if disabled, ensure no third-party antivirus is conflicting.

definition: a software-based firewall included with windows that filters network traffic based on rules
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Applications cannot communicate over the network, or ports that should be open are blocked.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the command “wf.msc” to open the advanced firewall settings and inspect the “Inbound” and “Outbound” rules to ensure the necessary traffic is permitted.

definition: the security framework used to manage identities resources and communication within a windows-based environment e g domain or workgroup
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Inability to join a domain, authentication failures, or resource access errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify DNS (Domain Name System) settings, check the computer’s trust relationship with the domain, and review event logs for Kerberos or authentication-related errors.

definition: security measures applied to wi-fi networks to prevent unauthorized access and eavesdropping including encryption and authentication protocols
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unauthorized users on the network, slow performance due to rogue device interference, or weak encryption alerts.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Upgrade to WPA3 (Wi-Fi Protected Access 3), use a hidden SSID (Service Set Identifier) if necessary (though limited effectiveness), and implement MAC (Media Access Control) address filtering.

definition: files generated by an os operating system or network appliance that record authentication events authorization attempts and other critical security-related activities to provide an audit trail
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Security event logs are full and no longer recording, critical security audits fail to capture unauthorized login attempts, or the log file itself is corrupted.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the “Event Viewer” by executing the command “eventvwr.msc”, navigate to “Windows Logs > Security”, check the log size settings, and increase the maximum log size or configure “Overwrite events as needed” if log rotation is not functioning.

definition: a settings interface in windows that allows users to define the security zone e g internet local intranet of a website determining the level of active content such as scripts and activex controls that the browser will execute
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Websites are blocked from executing necessary scripts, browsers display constant permission prompts, or sites that should be restricted are allowed to execute untrusted code.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Control Panel > Internet Options”, go to the “Security” tab, select the appropriate zone, click “Custom level”, and reset to the “Medium-high” default or explicitly enable/disable required components based on your organization's security policy.

definition: a personal safety technique used by technicians to prevent esd electrostatic discharge from damaging sensitive electronic components by creating a continuous electrical path between the technician and the grounded chassis of the equipment
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Components fail unexpectedly after handling, or micro-arcing occurs, causing intermittent system resets or hardware malfunctions.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Always wear an ESD (Electrostatic Discharge) wrist strap connected to the metal chassis of the device, or frequently touch a bare metal part of the PC case while working to maintain a neutral electrical potential.

definition: a legacy physical communication method using a serial interface such as rs-232 to transmit data sequentially one bit at a time often used for configuring networking hardware like routers and switches
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Inability to communicate with console ports, corrupted text during configuration sessions, or the device not being recognized by the terminal emulator.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify cable integrity, ensure the baud rate settings in your terminal emulation software (e.g., PuTTY) match the device specifications (commonly 9600), and use a null-modem adapter if connecting two DTE (Data Terminal Equipment) devices directly.

definition: dedicated computers or software instances that provide centralized services data or resources to other computers clients on a network
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Clients are unable to access network shares, internet connectivity is lost, or authentication requests are being timed out across the network.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the server’s physical connectivity, verify that critical services (e.g., DNS - Domain Name System, DHCP - Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) are running in the “Services” console, and examine the server event logs for hardware or application-level errors.

word: Servers: AAA (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting) servers
definition: a framework that manages network access by verifying user identities authentication determining permitted actions authorization and logging user activity accounting
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users are unable to connect to the network, permissions are inconsistently applied, or accounting records are missing.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify network connectivity between the client and the AAA (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting) server, check the shared secret keys, and review the server logs to identify which phase (Authentication, Authorization, or Accounting) is failing.

definition: a server responsible for verifying the credentials e g username password tokens provided by a client to grant access to network resources
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Widespread login failures, or error messages indicating that the authentication domain controller is unreachable.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the command “ping” to check connectivity to the server, ensure the clock is synced via NTP (Network Time Protocol), and check that the “Kerberos” or “LDAP” (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) services are functioning correctly.

word: Servers: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) servers
definition: a network service that automatically assigns ip internet protocol addresses subnet masks and default gateways to client devices
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Clients receive an “APIPA” (Automatic Private IP Addressing) address (169.254.x.x) or cannot connect to the network.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) scope has available addresses, run “ipconfig /release” and “ipconfig /renew” on the client, and check that the “DHCP Server” service is running on the host.

definition: a hierarchical system that resolves human-readable domain names e g www example com into machine-readable ip internet protocol addresses
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users cannot browse websites by name, but can connect using IP (Internet Protocol) addresses directly.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Test resolution using the command “nslookup” or “dig”, clear the local DNS (Domain Name System) cache using “ipconfig /flushdns”, and verify that the client is pointing to the correct DNS (Domain Name System) server IP.

definition: a centralized server that manages and provides access to files and folders for users across a network
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users report 'Access Denied' errors, slow file transfer speeds, or files becoming 'read-only' unexpectedly.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check disk quota limits, verify NTFS (New Technology File System) and share-level permissions, and ensure the server has sufficient storage capacity.

definition: a server that handles the sending receiving and storage of email messages using protocols like smtp simple mail transfer protocol imap internet message access protocol and pop3 post office protocol version 3
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Emails are stuck in the outbox, users cannot download mail, or authentication fails during client-to-server connection.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check for correct port configurations (e.g., 25, 465, 587, 993), ensure the mail server service is active, and check for blocklists that might be preventing email delivery.

definition: a dedicated device or server role that manages print jobs for multiple clients allowing them to queue and process documents for network printers
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Print jobs are stuck in the queue, printers appear 'Offline,' or users receive driver-related errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Restart the “Print Spooler” service using the command “net stop spooler” followed by “net start spooler”, and verify that the printer driver is correctly installed on the server.

definition: a server that acts as an intermediary for requests from clients seeking resources from other servers often used for caching and content filtering
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Internet connectivity is blocked, or users are receiving errors regarding 'Proxy Authentication Required.'
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify browser proxy settings in “Internet Options > Connections > LAN settings”, and ensure the proxy server is reachable via the network.

word: Servers: RADIUS (Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service) servers
definition: a networking protocol providing centralized aaa authentication authorization and accounting management for computers to connect and use a network service commonly used with wi-fi
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Wireless clients cannot authenticate, or the AP (Access Point) shows it cannot communicate with the RADIUS (Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service) server.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the shared secret key on both the client (AP) and the RADIUS (Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service) server, and check the logs for failed authentication requests.

definition: a type of proxy server that sits in front of web servers and forwards client requests to those web servers often used for load balancing and ssl secure sockets layer termination
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Web applications are inaccessible, or clients receive '502 Bad Gateway' errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the connectivity between the reverse proxy and the backend web servers, verify that the backend services are running, and inspect the proxy’s error logs for misconfigured forwarding rules.

definition: a centralized server that collects and stores log files from various network devices e g switches routers firewalls to simplify troubleshooting and security monitoring
ERROR SYMPTOMS: No logs are being received from network devices, or the syslog storage drive is full.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify that the network devices are configured to send logs to the server’s IP address, check that the syslog port (typically UDP 514) is open, and ensure the server has enough storage capacity.

word: Servers: TACACS+ (Terminal Access Controller Access-Control System Plus) servers
definition: a protocol developed by cisco that handles aaa authentication authorization and accounting for remote administrative access to network devices
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Administrators cannot log into network devices using centralized credentials.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the connection between the networking device and the TACACS+ (Terminal Access Controller Access-Control System Plus) server, verify the shared secret, and check if the device is correctly configured to use TACACS+ (Terminal Access Controller Access-Control System Plus) as the primary authentication method.

definition: a physical server running software that allows it to host multiple virtual server instances vms each with its own os operating system and resources
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Virtual machines are inaccessible, or the host server is showing high resource utilization, causing the guest VMs to hang.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the hypervisor management console for error alerts, verify hardware resource availability, and ensure the virtual network switch settings are correct.

definition: a server that uses http hypertext transfer protocol or https hypertext transfer protocol secure to serve web pages to clients
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Websites are 'down' (e.g., 404 or 500 errors), or the web server is unresponsive to browser requests.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check that the web server service (e.g., Apache, IIS - Internet Information Services) is running, ensure port 80/443 is open on the firewall, and inspect the web server error logs.

definition: background processes in an os operating system that provide specific functionality such as network connectivity printing or security without a user interface
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Features like networking, audio, or printing are not functioning, often accompanied by 'The service is not running' error messages.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the “Services” management console by executing the command “services.msc”, locate the problematic service, check its status, and click “Start” or “Restart” if it has stopped.

definition: a section in the windows task manager that provides a list of all currently running services allowing users to start stop or view the status of background processes
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A system feature is failing, and it is unclear if the underlying service is currently running.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Press “Ctrl + Shift + Esc” to open Task Manager, navigate to the “Services” tab, look for the service status, right-click the service, and select “Start” or “Stop” to troubleshoot the behavior.

TROUBLESHOOTING: Log into the targeted switches via a secure shell console configuration layer, verify that the active SNMP daemon service is running, ensure the configured read/write "Community String" credentials or Version 3 cryptographic user parameters exactly match the central monitoring console settings, and confirm UDP (User Datagram Protocol) ports “161” and “162” are open through local firewalls.

definition: a critical primary domain name system dns zone file record that documents foundational administrative metadata regarding the hosting zone including the primary authoritative name server the zone administrator s email and zone refresh timers
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Secondary backup name servers fail to sync zone updates from the primary master directory node, leading to stale name resolution states across the corporate enterprise.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Launch the diagnostic console terminal line interface and execute the lookup lookup command string “nslookup -type=soa example.com”; examine the output serial number parameter to confirm it increments sequentially with every modification to verify that database synchronization is occurring correctly.

definition: a deceptive manipulation technique where an attacker exploits human psychology trust or social norms to coerce individuals into divulging confidential information bypassing traditional network security barriers or performing unauthorized actions
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Employees report receiving highly convincing but unsolicited emails asking for credentials, unauthorized visitors are found in sensitive areas claiming to be maintenance workers, or strange account login activity occurs from suspicious locations despite no system compromise.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Implement mandatory, recurring security awareness training, establish strict verification protocols for any request involving sensitive data or physical access, and utilize multi-factor authentication (MFA) to ensure that even compromised credentials cannot grant total system access.

definition: a set of standardized defensive protocols and behavioral guidelines designed to harden human assets against social engineering attacks emphasizing skepticism verification and procedural adherence
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Security audits reveal that employees consistently use weak passwords, post sensitive data on public social media platforms, or share login badges, indicating a lack of a ingrained security culture.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Enforce strict “clean desk” policies, utilize automated phishing simulation tests to measure personnel awareness, and standardize a "verify-before-trust" procedure for all incoming requests, particularly those demanding urgency or secrecy.

definition: a cryptographic attack method where an adversary systematically attempts every possible combination of characters in an exhaustive sequence until the correct password encryption key or pin is identified
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Security logs display an overwhelming number of failed login attempts for a single user account in a very short window, or network monitoring tools identify a massive spike in authentication packets.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Configure an account lockout policy that disables user access after a defined number of failed attempts (e.g., 5 failures in 10 minutes), implement CAPTCHA (Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart) on login portals, and enforce complex, long-length password requirements.

definition: an advanced attack methodology aimed at uncovering hidden information or breaking encrypted data by identifying structural weaknesses mathematical patterns or flaws within the encryption algorithm implementation rather than just guessing the key
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Encrypted data streams appear perfectly formed but sensitive contents are being leaked or intercepted, or security tools indicate that older, vulnerable encryption standards (like WEP or DES) are being actively exploited.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Immediately upgrade all encryption standards to modern, robust protocols (such as AES - Advanced Encryption Standard), decommission deprecated ciphers, and ensure that security patches for cryptographic libraries are applied across all hardware nodes.

word: Social engineering: DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) attacks
definition: a malicious campaign where an attacker uses an array of compromised systems a botnet to flood a target server service or network infrastructure with an overwhelming volume of traffic rendering it unavailable to legitimate users
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Web servers become unresponsive or time out constantly, network bandwidth consumption reaches near-capacity despite normal usage levels, and monitoring systems alert on abnormal traffic spikes from thousands of disparate global IP addresses.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Deploy traffic-filtering services (such as an upstream scrubbing service), utilize a Content Delivery Network (CDN) to distribute load, and configure firewall rules to rate-limit traffic from high-risk origin subnets or countries.

definition: a targeted password-cracking technique where an attacker uses a predefined list of words common passwords and variations the dictionary to systematically test against authentication systems often exploiting weak user-chosen passwords
ERROR SYMPTOMS: User account lockouts occur frequently, or forensic analysis of compromised accounts reveals that passwords were common terms found in public wordlists.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Mandate the use of long passphrases instead of simple dictionary-word passwords, enable multi-factor authentication (MFA), and implement a "banned password list" that prevents users from selecting commonly compromised strings.

word: Social engineering: DoS (Denial of Service) attacks
definition: a singular-source attack designed to consume a target system's resources cpu ram or bandwidth causing the service or device to crash or become so slow that it can no longer process legitimate user requests
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A specific network service (like a printer or local file server) suddenly goes offline or exhibits massive latency spikes, while other network devices remain perfectly functional.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Identify the source IP address of the traffic stream, block the originating address via firewall rules, and investigate the host to identify if a specific process is being targeted by a malformed request.

definition: a physical reconnaissance technique where an attacker sifts through physical trash discarded hard drives or recycled paper documents to find discarded account numbers passwords project plans or sensitive corporate pii personally identifiable information
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Information that was never leaked digitally—such as internal company organizational charts or secret project names—is suddenly appearing in public or being used by external competitors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Mandate the use of high-security shredders for all paper documentation, perform physical destruction (degaussing or physical crushing) of old hard drives and storage media before disposal, and secure trash collection areas.

definition: a rogue wireless access point ap configured to masquerade as a legitimate network using the same ssid - service set identifier designed to trick unsuspecting users into connecting so the attacker can intercept their traffic
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users report being disconnected from the "office" Wi-Fi and then prompted to re-enter their credentials on an unfamiliar or unencrypted login page, or network monitoring tools detect a new, rogue AP with a high signal strength mimicking the company SSID.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Conduct periodic wireless site surveys to locate unauthorized APs, implement 802.1X certificate-based authentication to prevent clients from connecting to rogue APs, and educate users to only connect to known, secured wireless segments.

definition: the act of pretending to be someone else usually a person of authority an it technician or a vendor to manipulate a target into providing information or performing an action they wouldn't normally authorize
ERROR SYMPTOMS: An employee receives an urgent call from someone claiming to be "the IT administrator from head office" demanding their login credentials to "fix a server issue," or someone shows up at the door claiming to be a delivery person to gain access to a secure facility.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Establish a policy that IT staff never request passwords over the phone or email, implement badge-based access control, and confirm identities by calling back the person at a verified, official contact number.

definition: a category of web application vulnerabilities where an attacker provides untrusted input that is processed by an interpreter as part of a command or query causing the system to execute unintended operations
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Database tables are corrupted, unauthorized users gain administrative rights, or an application displays erratic data that differs from what is stored in the database.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Implement strict input validation and sanitization for all user-entered data, utilize parameterized queries (prepared statements) in application development to separate code from data, and use web application firewalls (WAF) to filter malicious requests.

definition: malicious activity carried out by individuals who have authorized access to a company's systems such as current or former employees contractors or business associates who exploit that access to steal data or sabotage infrastructure
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Sensitive data is exfiltrated during non-working hours, files are inexplicably deleted, or access permissions are suddenly changed to give users administrative rights they do not require for their role.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Apply the "Principle of Least Privilege" (PoLP) to ensure users have access only to what they need, implement robust logging and auditing of all administrative actions, and perform thorough offboarding processes for terminated personnel to revoke all access immediately.

definition: the process of recovering passwords from stored data like database hashes or by intercepting network traffic often using automated software rainbow tables or brute-force methods
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A large database hash file is found on a user's machine, or internal security scanners report that user accounts have been compromised using patterns derived from internal databases.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Store passwords using salted, slow-hashing algorithms (like Argon2 or bcrypt) to make cracking difficult, enforce regular password rotation, and monitor systems for unauthorized authentication attempts or the presence of cracking software tools.

definition: a fraudulent communication method usually email where an attacker poses as a reputable entity like a bank or it department to trick the recipient into clicking a malicious link downloading a file or entering credentials on a fake website
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users report receiving suspicious emails with misspelled sender addresses, generic greetings, and urgent requests to click links, or browser security filters warn that a site is a known phishing domain.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Deploy email filtering solutions that automatically identify and quarantine suspicious links and attachments, enable DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance) to prevent domain spoofing, and educate users on identifying phishing red flags.

definition: a physical security breach where an unauthorized individual follows an authorized person into a restricted area often by catching a closing door without the authorized person's direct knowledge or consent
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unauthorized persons are found in secure server rooms, or facility security logs show multiple entries for a single badge swipe.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Install mantraps (two-door entry systems where the first must close before the second opens), use turnstiles that allow only one person per entry, and train employees to never hold secure doors open for others.

definition: the act of creating a fabricated scenario the pretext to engage a victim and increase the likelihood that they will share information or perform an action such as pretending to be a bank auditor needing account confirmation
ERROR SYMPTOMS: An employee feels pressured into performing an unusual, highly sensitive action based on a story they were told by someone over the phone, and they report feeling confused or coerced afterward.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Require personnel to verify any request for sensitive information through a secondary communication channel, establish strict corporate procedures for identity confirmation, and train staff to recognize common high-pressure social engineering tactics.

definition: a simple reconnaissance method where an attacker gains information by peeking over a user s shoulder to see passwords pins or confidential data displayed on a monitor or keyboard
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unauthorized access occurs despite strong password policies, often occurring in public locations like coffee shops or in high-traffic office areas.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Apply privacy screen filters to monitors to narrow the viewing angle, position computers away from windows or high-traffic corridors, and instruct employees to lock their screens (Windows Key + “L”) whenever they leave their desk.

definition: the act of falsifying data such as an ip address email sender address or caller id to disguise the origin of a communication and gain the victim's trust
ERROR SYMPTOMS: An email appears to come from the CEO but contains suspicious links, or an internal server reports connection attempts from an IP address that should not exist on the local network.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Implement email authentication protocols (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), use network ingress/egress filtering to block spoofed IP addresses, and configure firewalls to prevent internal source addresses from appearing on external interfaces.

definition: a specific type of injection attack where malicious sql code is inserted into input fields causing the backend database to execute unauthorized commands which may result in data theft or system destruction
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Database records are altered or deleted without explanation, and logs indicate that application inputs were used to gain unauthorized access to the table structure.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements), enforce strict input validation, and ensure that the database service account has only the minimum necessary privileges required for the application to function.

definition: a physical security vulnerability where an unauthorized person tags along with an authorized person through a secure entrance often with the authorized person's knowledge and permission e g holding the door
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unknown individuals are observed in offices during business hours, or security cameras reveal individuals frequently following employees through secure badge-access doors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Utilize mantraps, enforce "no-tailgating" policies, and promote a culture where employees feel empowered to challenge anyone who does not have visible identification.

definition: an attack where the perpetrator injects malicious client-side scripts into a trusted website which then execute in the browsers of other users allowing the attacker to steal cookies session tokens or capture keystrokes
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users report that they are being logged out of sessions unexpectedly, or that they are being redirected to suspicious websites while browsing a legitimate corporate portal.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Sanitize all user-supplied data in web applications, implement Content Security Policy (CSP) headers to restrict which scripts can execute, and use secure cookies (HttpOnly) to prevent script access to sensitive session data.

definition: a sophisticated attack that exploits a software or hardware vulnerability that is unknown to the vendor and for which no patch or remediation exists yet
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Systems are compromised despite being fully patched, and antivirus or intrusion detection systems fail to trigger any alerts because the exploit is entirely new.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Employ behavior-based monitoring and Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS) that look for anomalous activity rather than known signatures, maintain robust offline backups, and implement strict network segmentation to limit the blast radius if a system is compromised.

definition: a computer or device that has been compromised by malware allowing an attacker to control it remotely often as part of a botnet without the owner's knowledge usually to perform ddos attacks or send spam
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A workstation exhibits unexplained high CPU or network utilization, or internet connectivity is intermittently lost as the system participates in an attack.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Perform a full system scan using updated antivirus/antimalware tools, disconnect the device from the network to stop the C2 (Command and Control) traffic, and re-image the system to ensure no rootkits remain.

definition: physical mounting slots on a motherboard that hold the cpu central processing unit in place providing the electrical interface for communication between the processor and the rest of the system
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The system fails to boot (No-POST), or the user experiences random system crashes due to improper thermal contact or loose electrical pins within the CPU socket.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Inspect the socket for bent or broken pins (especially on LGA - Land Grid Array sockets), ensure the CPU is seated perfectly, and verify that the thermal interface material is applied evenly to ensure efficient heat transfer.

definition: a cpu socket type where the pins are located on the motherboard socket rather than on the cpu package itself requiring extreme caution during installation to avoid damaging the delicate motherboard pins
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The computer won't turn on or consistently hangs at the BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) screen, often due to a pin that was bent during installation.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Carefully remove the CPU and inspect the motherboard socket with a magnifying glass for any misaligned pins; if pins are bent, use a fine needle to gently realign them, or replace the motherboard if the pins are broken.

definition: a cpu socket type where the pins are located on the underside of the cpu itself which slide into corresponding holes on the motherboard socket this design is generally more robust regarding pin alignment than lga models
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The CPU fails to seat fully in the socket, or the system does not boot because the CPU pins are bent or missing.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Carefully inspect the CPU pins for any bending, use a small tool or mechanical pencil to straighten bent pins, and ensure the retention lever is fully locked to ensure complete contact.

definition: a fundamental networking communication concept where a source and destination port act as sockets that allow processes to communicate over the network reliably using a persistent three-way handshake connection
ERROR SYMPTOMS: An application reports "Connection refused" or "Socket error," meaning it cannot establish a valid communication channel with the destination service.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the command “netstat -an” to view the status of all active connections, verify that the application is listening on the correct port, and ensure no local or network firewall rules are blocking the communication socket.

definition: a compact memory module standard used primarily in laptops mini-pcs and embedded systems where physical space is at a premium and standard dimm dual in-line memory module modules are too large
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The laptop emits a series of memory-related beeps at startup, or the system crashes frequently when running memory-intensive applications.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the SODIMM module is firmly snapped into the slot, test with one module at a time to identify a faulty unit, and clean the gold contacts with an eraser or isopropyl alcohol if the system fails to recognize the RAM.

definition: a virtual or digital version of a physical security token typically provided as an app on a smartphone that generates temporary single-use authentication codes otp - one-time passwords for multi-factor authentication
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The user is unable to generate the required OTP code, or the code entered is consistently rejected as invalid.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify that the device time is synchronized accurately with network time (NTP), as time-based tokens rely on synchronized clocks, and re-sync the token app with the authentication server if clock drift has occurred.

definition: security applications designed to detect block and remove malicious code malware viruses spyware from smartphones and tablets which is essential as mobile devices become primary targets for data theft
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The mobile device behaves illegally or sluggishly, battery drains rapidly, or unexpected applications appear on the device home screen.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Install a reputable mobile security app from the official vendor store (Google Play or Apple App Store), perform a full system scan, and uninstall any suspicious or unverified third-party applications.

definition: software where the source code is kept proprietary and is not available for public modification audit or redistribution meaning only the vendor can release updates or fix bugs
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A system-wide performance issue occurs that cannot be investigated because the underlying logic of the software is invisible to the administrator.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Contact the vendor's technical support, check the vendor's knowledge base for patches, and ensure the latest version of the application is installed according to the vendor's release notes.

definition: centralized tools used by it administrators to monitor update and manage the health and configuration of multiple networked desktop computers e g microsoft endpoint configuration manager
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Updates fail to deploy to client machines, or remote management tasks (like inventory scanning) return "Host unreachable" errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the connectivity between the management server and the client machine, verify the management agent service is running on the client, and check firewall logs to ensure management ports are open.

definition: the legal agreement that governs the use distribution and modification of software defining how many devices or users are authorized to use a specific installation
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The application displays "License expired" or "Activation failed" errors, or the software suddenly limits functionality because it detects an unauthorized number of concurrent instances.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Audit the number of current installations, enter the valid license key provided by the vendor, and use license management software to ensure compliance if the organization is approaching its usage limits.

definition: software that is distributed with its source code available allowing anyone to inspect modify and improve the software fostering community-driven development and transparency
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A critical bug is discovered, or the software does not work as expected with specific hardware configurations.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the project's community forums for bug reports and fixes, contribute to the community by submitting a patch, or compile a custom version of the software with the necessary tweaks to meet your specific requirements.

definition: an architectural approach to networking that allows network control to be programmed centrally separating the network's control logic the brain from the hardware the switches and routers
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Network traffic is not being routed as defined by the policy, or the SDN controller loses communication with the network hardware, leading to broken data paths.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the communication link between the SDN controller and the forwarding devices, verify the routing policies are correctly loaded in the controller, and reset the control connection if the SDN switch appears "disconnected."

definition: the integrated feature in macos that automatically checks for downloads and installs system-level updates patches and security improvements from apple
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The operating system warns that security updates are missing, or system features (like AirDrop or iCloud) stop working because the system version is outdated.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “System Settings > General > Software Update” to force a manual check, and ensure the system has a stable internet connection if the update progress bar remains stuck.

definition: external or internal hardware components on a wireless router that emit and receive radio waves determining the signal coverage quality and directionality of the network
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Wi-Fi signal is weak in certain parts of the home or office, or users report frequent disconnections when they move away from the router.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Adjust the antenna angle to optimize coverage (if omnidirectional), upgrade to higher-gain antennas if distance is an issue, and ensure the router is placed in a central, elevated location away from metal obstructions.

definition: a networking device that allows wi-fi devices to connect to a wired network effectively acting as the bridge for wireless client communication
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Devices can see the wireless network name (SSID) but cannot successfully connect or receive an IP address.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Power cycle the AP, verify that the wired Ethernet cable connection is intact, and check the AP's DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) settings to ensure it is correctly assigning IP addresses to clients.

word: SOHO (Small Office/Home Office) networks: Guest networks
definition: a separate isolated wireless network broadcasted by a soho router specifically for guests which provides internet access while preventing users from seeing or accessing the internal corporate or home network
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A guest is able to see internal file shares or network-attached storage, indicating that the guest isolation feature is failing or not configured.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Access the router’s wireless security settings, ensure the “Guest Network” option is toggled to “Enabled seasonings”, and verify that the “Enable isolation” or “AP isolation” checkbox is selected to segregate guest traffic from the primary network.

word: SOHO (Small Office/Home Office) networks: IP filtering
definition: a security feature on soho routers that allows the administrator to block or permit traffic based on the source or destination ip address providing basic firewall capabilities
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Specific internet services are inaccessible, or a machine that should be restricted still has full access to the internet.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Log into the router's web interface, navigate to the “Firewall” or “Access Control” section, review the existing IP filter rules for incorrect entries, and update the rules to permit or block the target IP address as required.

definition: the most widely used version of the internet protocol utilizing 32-bit addresses to identify devices on a network usually represented in decimal format e g 192 168 1 1
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Network conflicts occur where two devices claim the same IP address, or devices are unable to communicate due to an incorrect subnet mask configuration.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the command “ipconfig /release” and “ipconfig /renew” to refresh the local IP, and ensure the router’s DHCP scope has sufficient addresses available for all connected clients.

definition: the newer generation of the internet protocol utilizing 128-bit addresses to provide a virtually infinite supply of unique ip addresses intended to replace the exhausted ipv4 address space
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A device is not reachable, or modern network applications fail to initialize because the router or ISP (Internet Service Provider) does not support IPv6 properly.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify that the router has IPv6 enabled and that the ISP provides an IPv6 prefix delegation, and check client settings to ensure they are configured to obtain an IPv6 address automatically.

word: SOHO (Small Office/Home Office) networks: MAC filtering
definition: a security feature that allows the router to restrict network access to devices based on their unique physical hardware address mac - media access control address
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A legitimate device cannot join the wireless network despite having the correct password, or an unauthorized device has successfully gained network access.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the router's "Allowed" or "Blocked" MAC address list, add the device's MAC address if it’s currently blocked, and remember that MAC addresses can be spoofed, so do not rely on this as a primary security method.

word: SOHO (Small Office/Home Office) networks: Radio power levels
definition: the configurable intensity of the wi-fi signal emitted by the wireless router lowering the power can restrict signal coverage to a specific room preventing unauthorized access from outside the office
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Signal coverage is insufficient in certain rooms, or the signal is so strong that it extends into public spaces, increasing the surface area for potential attacks.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Access the router’s wireless settings, adjust the "Transmit Power" (often listed as a percentage or in dBm), and perform a signal strength test from various locations to strike the right balance between coverage and security.

definition: the central networking device in a soho environment that connects the internal local network to the internet performing routing firewalling and wireless access functionality
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Internet connectivity is completely lost, internal devices cannot communicate, or the management interface is inaccessible.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Perform a hard reset by holding the physical reset button for 10-15 seconds (after backing up settings), check cable connections to the ISP modem, and verify that the WAN (Wide Area Network) port has an active internet connection.

definition: the overall practice of hardening the soho network by implementing strong encryption wpa3 changing default management credentials disabling unused ports and segmenting guest traffic
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Network logs reveal unauthorized access attempts, or performance issues are occurring due to malicious traffic floods from infected internal devices.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Change the default administrator password immediately, disable WPS (Wi-Fi Protected Setup), enable WPA3 (Wi-Fi Protected Access 3) encryption, and keep the router firmware updated to prevent exploitation of known vulnerabilities.

word: SOHO (Small Office/Home Office) networks: Static IP addresses
definition: a fixed ip address manually assigned to a device like a printer or server rather than one dynamically assigned by a dhcp server ensuring the device is always reachable at the same address
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A network device becomes unreachable because the DHCP pool moved, or an IP address conflict occurs because another device was manually assigned the same static IP.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the device's network settings to confirm the static IP is within the correct subnet and outside the range of addresses assigned by the DHCP server to avoid conflicts.

definition: a disturbance generated by external electromagnetic sources such as microwave ovens fluorescent lights or high-voltage power lines that disrupts the transmission of data over copper-based network cabling
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users experience intermittent network packet loss, exceptionally slow transfer speeds, or complete connection drops, specifically when near large electrical appliances or industrial equipment.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Replace unshielded UTP (Unshielded Twisted Pair) cabling with STP (Shielded Twisted Pair) or fiber optic cables, route network cables away from high-voltage electrical conduits, and use high-quality, grounded network hardware.

definition: a set of step-by-step written instructions compiled by an organization to help workers carry out complex routine operations ensuring consistency compliance and quality in technical task completion
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Technicians provide inconsistent fixes for identical issues, security configurations vary between different workstations, or a high rate of human error occurs during routine hardware maintenance.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Document all technical workflows clearly, require mandatory review cycles for procedures, and ensure that all IT (Information Technology) staff follow the current approved version found in the organization's central knowledge base.

definition: the windows interface that allows for the management and configuration of audio output devices speakers headphones and input devices microphones including sample rates levels and playback defaults
ERROR SYMPTOMS: No sound is produced by the workstation, the system default microphone is not capturing input, or audio intermittently cuts out after installing new software.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Navigate to the “Control Panel > Sound”, verify that the correct device is set as the “Default Device”, ensure that the volume levels are not muted in the “Levels” tab, and check the “Advanced” tab to restore default audio sample formats.

definition: an internal or external hardware component responsible for converting digital audio signals into analog signals for speakers digital-to-analog converter or dac and vice-versa for microphones
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Distorted or static-filled audio output, the sound card is missing from the “Device Manager” list, or the system crashes (BSOD - Blue Screen of Death) whenever audio-intensive applications are launched.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Reseat the sound card in its PCIe (Peripheral Component Interconnect Express) slot, update the device drivers via the manufacturer's website, or test the sound card in a different motherboard slot to rule out a faulty bus port.

definition: a security appliance or cloud-based service that sits in front of an email server to inspect incoming mail traffic for signatures heuristics and ip reputation associated with unsolicited or malicious spam emails
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users report a sudden influx of junk mail reaching their inbox, or legitimate business emails are being incorrectly quarantined and blocked.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Review the gateway's quarantine logs for blocked messages, update the spam filtering rules or “allow lists” for specific domains, and verify the DNS (Domain Name System) SPF (Sender Policy Framework) records are correctly configured.

definition: keys found on keyboards typically labeled fn that when used in combination with other keys like f1 f12 trigger specific system hardware adjustments such as screen brightness volume control or wireless radio toggling
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The user cannot increase screen brightness, turn off the touchpad, or toggle Wi-Fi, despite the system functioning normally otherwise.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure that the manufacturer’s keyboard utility software or driver is installed, check the BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) settings to see if the “Fn” key behavior is set to “Multimedia” or “Standard Function Key” mode.

definition: a broad measurement of performance metrics for system components encompassing data throughput clock cycles and communication frequencies between hardware subsystems
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Overall system performance is sluggish, files take longer than expected to move between disks, or network performance is bottlenecked compared to the rated hardware capacity.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check task manager for high I/O (Input/Output) wait times, compare current hardware speeds against the manufacturer's specification sheets, and use benchmarking tools to isolate whether the slowdown is caused by the bus, the CPU, or the storage medium.

definition: the rate at which data is transferred over the computer's internal buses such as the front-side bus or local buses which dictates the communication speed between the cpu and other components like ram random access memory
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Memory latency issues or system hangs under heavy load when the bus speed is mismatched or improperly configured in the BIOS.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Enter the BIOS/UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) and ensure that the bus speed is set to “Auto” or that it matches the RAM’s rated XMP (Extreme Memory Profile) frequency to ensure optimal, stable synchronization.

definition: the frequency at which a processor or component executes internal operations usually measured in ghz gigahertz representing how many cycles occur per second
ERROR SYMPTOMS: CPU throttling occurs, where the processor drastically reduces its speed to prevent overheating, causing noticeable system lag and application unresponsiveness.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Clean dust from the heatsink/fan assembly, reapply thermal paste to ensure effective heat dissipation, and use a tool like “CPU-Z” to verify the current frequency is not stuck in a low-power state.

definition: the operational frequency of the pathways on the motherboard that connect the cpu memory and peripheral expansion slots determining the maximum throughput for data traveling through the system board
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Peripheral devices (like high-speed storage controllers) run at lower speeds than rated, or the system crashes when multiple high-bandwidth devices are used simultaneously.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify motherboard firmware updates, ensure all memory modules are seated in the correct channels to support dual-channel or quad-channel bus configurations, and confirm that all expansion cards are seated in slots that match their rated speed.

definition: the speed at which data travels over a network usually measured in mbps megabits per second or gbps gigabits per second affected by physical layer cabling hardware configuration and congestion
ERROR SYMPTOMS: File copies over the LAN (Local Area Network) are significantly slower than expected, or network-intensive applications report frequent time-outs.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the command “ping” to check for latency, use the command “iperf” to test bandwidth capacity between two nodes, and verify that all switches and network interface cards (NICs) are negotiating at the intended full-duplex speed (e.g., 1000 Mbps).

definition: the data transmission capability of copper cables used in local networks classified by categories e g cat5e cat6 that define their maximum frequency and data speed
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The network performance does not reach the expected gigabit speeds, or the connection frequently drops back to 100 Mbps (Fast Ethernet).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Inspect cables for damage or sharp bends, verify the cable category meets the required standard for the network (e.g., Cat6 for Gigabit), and ensure the cable length does not exceed 100 meters, which leads to signal degradation.
