definition: a dns-based email authentication method that specifies which mail servers are authorized to send email on behalf of a specific domain helping to prevent email spoofing
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Legitimate emails sent from the organization are being marked as spam or rejected by external mail servers.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Access the domain’s DNS records, verify that the TXT (Text) record containing the “v=spf1” entry includes all authorized mail server IP addresses, and use an online validator tool to ensure the record is formatted correctly.

definition: the visual icon that appears in macos when an application or the os becomes unresponsive indicating that the system is waiting for a process to complete before it can continue
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The cursor turns into a multicolored rotating circle, and the user is unable to click buttons or interact with the active application window.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Force-quit the hanging application by pressing “Command + Option + Escape”, select the application, and choose “Force Quit”; if the entire system hangs, press and hold the power button to perform a hard reboot.

definition: the process of dividing a single logical or physical storage volume into multiple partitions or separate volumes to organize data separate os files or increase manageability
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A storage volume runs out of space, or a single partition containing both the OS and personal files becomes corrupted, risking the loss of all data on the disk.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Disk Management” (on Windows), right-click the volume, select “Shrink Volume” to create unallocated space, and then create a new partition from that space formatted with an appropriate file system (like NTFS - New Technology File System).

definition: instances where a computer turns off unexpectedly without a standard shutdown command typically as a protection mechanism against thermal runaway or power failure
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The PC suddenly goes black and loses power while the user is working, or it reboots on its own without any warning.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Inspect the PSU (Power Supply Unit) for proper voltage output, monitor CPU temperatures, check the “Event Viewer” in Windows for “Kernel-Power 41” errors, and ensure the wall outlet/UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) is providing stable power.

definition: a deceptive attack where a perpetrator masquerades as a trusted entity such as an ip address email sender or mac address to gain unauthorized access or trick a user into performing a malicious action
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unusual login locations appear in server logs, or email communications arrive with forged headers claiming to originate from internal executives or trusted partners.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Implement security protocols such as SPF, DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail), and DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance) for email, and use ingress/egress filtering on routers to prevent spoofed packets from entering or leaving the network.

definition: a process where the os intercepts print jobs sent by applications stores them in a temporary file the spool and feeds them to the printer at a rate it can handle preventing applications from freezing while waiting for the printer
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Print jobs are stuck in the queue, “Print Spooler” service errors appear, or documents appear in the printer's display but never actually print.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the “Services” console, locate the “Print Spooler” service, right-click it, and select “Restart”; if that fails, navigate to “C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS” and delete any orphaned files in that folder.

definition: the built-in system-wide desktop search utility in macos that allows for rapid file indexing and retrieval as well as launching applications and performing calculations
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Search results are incomplete, the search index is corrupted, or the system experiences high CPU usage as Spotlight attempts to re-index the hard drive continuously.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Go to “System Settings > Siri & Spotlight > Spotlight Privacy”, add the hard drive to the exclusion list, remove it immediately after to force a re-index, and allow the system time to complete the background operation.

definition: a type of malicious software that installs itself on a device to secretly collect information about the user s activity such as browsing habits keystrokes or account credentials and reports it to a third party
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unexpected toolbars appear in browsers, web browser settings are modified without consent, the computer runs extremely slow, or excessive pop-up advertisements appear on the desktop.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Run a full scan with a trusted antimalware utility, check for and uninstall suspicious browser extensions, and reset the browser to its original default settings.

definition: a code injection technique where an attacker inserts malicious sql structured query language commands into input fields causing the database to execute unintended operations or reveal sensitive information
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unauthorized access to the database, unexpected data deletions, or application errors indicating an issue with database query syntax.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Implement parameterized queries (prepared statements) to isolate input from code, use input validation to sanitize data, and apply the "Principle of Least Privilege" (PoLP) to the database service account.

definition: a high-performance storage device that uses flash memory nand - negating and logic to store data providing significantly faster read write speeds and better durability than traditional hdd hard disk drives due to the absence of moving mechanical parts
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Extremely slow system response, intermittent read/write errors, or the system fails to boot because the controller on the SSD has failed.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Run the “CHKDSK” utility to check for file system errors, update the SSD firmware via the manufacturer's management software, and check the BIOS to ensure the SATA (Serial Advanced Technology Attachment) mode is set to AHCI (Advanced Host Controller Interface).

definition: a cryptographic network protocol used to operate network services securely over an unsecured network most commonly used for remote command-line login and remote command execution
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The user is unable to connect to a remote server, or “Connection refused” errors occur because the service is not running or the firewall is blocking port 22.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the SSH service is active on the target device by using the command “systemctl status sshd”, and ensure that port 22 is open on both the local and remote firewalls.

definition: the user-defined name of a wireless network which is broadcasted by an ap to identify the network changing this from the default factory name is a critical first step in securing a soho network
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Users are connecting to the wrong network, or the network name is the default factory setting (e.g., “Linksys”), making it easy for attackers to identify the router type.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Access the router’s web interface, navigate to the “Wireless” settings, update the SSID to a unique, non-identifying name, and save the configuration; all client devices will need to be reconnected to the new SSID.

definition: an optional security practice where the ap is configured to stop broadcasting its ssid requiring users to manually enter the exact network name on their devices to connect
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Devices cannot find the network in the list of available Wi-Fi networks, which is the expected result of disabling the broadcast.
TROUBLESHOOTING: If you need to reconnect, manually add the network profile in the OS by typing the SSID name, encryption type, and password; remember that this is "security through obscurity" and should not replace robust WPA3 (Wi-Fi Protected Access 3) encryption.

definition: the process of assigning a unique name to a wireless network which should be done without including any sensitive information such as the company name address or router model
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A public network named “Management_Server” is broadcasting, which provides an attacker with a high-value target and clues about the network's structure.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Rename the SSID to something generic and non-identifiable, such as “Guest_Net” or a project-specific name that does not disclose sensitive internal information.

definition: a session and user authentication service that permits a user to use one set of login credentials username and password to access multiple independent software systems minimizing credential fatigue
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The user cannot log into any linked applications, or the SSO token has expired, preventing access to resources even though the user is authenticated in the central directory.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the user's account status in the directory service (like Active Directory), ensure the system time on both the client and the authentication server is synchronized, and clear the local web browser cache if a session cookie is stale.

definition: a type of fiber optic connector that uses a bayonet-style twist-lock mechanism to secure the fiber cable commonly used in enterprise networking environments
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Loss of network signal, intermittent connection drops, or physical damage to the connector causing light leakage.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Disconnect the ST connector, inspect the tip for dirt or scratches, clean the fiber tip using a dedicated fiber-optic cleaning kit, and ensure the connector is fully locked into place by twisting it until it clicks.

definition: defined roles in a change management process such as the change requester the change advisory board and the implementer all of which are necessary to manage approve and track modifications to the environment
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Changes are made without approval, documentation is missing, or the wrong personnel are assigned to handle critical infrastructure updates.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Review the organization’s change management policy, ensure that every staff member clearly understands their assigned role, and document all changes in a central database or ticket management system.

definition: a user account type with limited permissions that prevents the user from making system-wide changes such as installing software changing critical os settings or modifying system files
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The user is unable to install necessary software or run specific diagnostic tools, resulting in “Access Denied” or “Permission Denied” errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: If the user requires higher privileges for their job role, temporarily assign them to the “Administrators” group or use the “Run as Administrator” feature, but always return them to a standard user account to maintain the principle of least privilege.

definition: a power-saving state sometimes called sleep that keeps the computer in a state where it consumes minimal power but can return to full operation near-instantaneously keeping open files and applications in ram
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The computer fails to “wake up” from standby, peripherals do not resume connectivity, or the computer unexpectedly wakes up on its own.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Update power management drivers in “Device Manager”, check the “Power Options” settings to disable “Wake on LAN” or USB wake events if they are causing unwanted activity, and run the “powercfg /lastwake” command to identify the device causing the issue.

definition: a network layout where all nodes are connected individually to a central connection point such as a switch or a hub meaning that if one cable fails only that node is disconnected from the network
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Multiple nodes are unreachable, indicating that the central switch may be failing or that a main trunk cable has been disconnected.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the lights on the central switch, verify that the uplink to the rest of the network is intact, and swap out the suspected faulty cables or switch ports to isolate the break.

definition: the primary graphical interface element in windows that serves as the central hub for launching applications accessing system settings and managing user files
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The menu does not open when clicked, search functionality within the menu is broken, or icons within the menu are missing.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Restart the “Windows Explorer” process in the “Task Manager”, run the “System File Checker” (the command “sfc /scannow”) to repair potentially corrupted OS files, or recreate the local user profile.

word: Starting up: Startup Repair, Windows RE (Recovery Environment)
definition: a windows feature designed to automatically diagnose and fix common issues that prevent the operating system from booting such as corrupted system files or missing boot configuration data
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The computer loops at the Windows logo, or a “Startup Repair” error screen appears, stating that Windows cannot boot.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Boot from Windows installation media, select “Repair your computer”, navigate to “Troubleshoot > Advanced Options > Startup Repair”, and allow the system to attempt an automatic scan and repair of the boot environment.

word: Starting up: Startup Settings, Windows RE (Recovery Environment)
definition: a specialized menu that allows users to access diagnostic modes such as safe mode that help troubleshoot and repair problems that occur during the windows boot process
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The system has frequent stop errors (BSOD) at startup or is infected with malware that is preventing the normal Windows shell from loading.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Access Windows RE by forcing a reboot three times during the boot cycle, go to “Troubleshoot > Advanced Options > Startup Settings”, click “Restart”, and select the number key corresponding to “Safe Mode” to enter the environment for troubleshooting.

word: Starting up: Startup tab, Task Manager
definition: a windows interface that lists all applications configured to run automatically when the user logs into the os allowing users to manage or disable them to improve boot times and system performance
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The system takes a long time to reach the desktop, or the computer is bogged down by unnecessary background processes immediately after logging in.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the “Task Manager” (Ctrl+Shift+Esc), navigate to the “Startup” tab, select the unnecessary applications, and click “Disable” to prevent them from launching at boot.

definition: the manual configuration of an ip address on a network device ensuring that the device maintains the same address on the network instead of receiving one dynamically from a dhcp dynamic host configuration protocol server
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The device is unreachable on the network because its IP address conflicts with another device, or it does not have the correct subnet mask/gateway information to access the internet.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Network and Sharing Center > Change adapter settings”, right-click the network adapter, select “Properties”, choose “Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4)”, click “Properties”, and manually enter the required IP address, subnet mask, and default gateway.

definition: a critical system failure alert in windows that occurs when the kernel detects an error from which it cannot safely recover usually caused by driver failures or hardware malfunctions
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The screen turns bright blue with a white error code (e.g., “IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL”) and the system instantly reboots.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Write down the specific error code, search the error on the Microsoft knowledge base, check for outdated drivers in “Device Manager”, and run a memory diagnostic test to ensure the RAM is not the source of the crash.

definition: the act of terminating a running application or process that has become unresponsive crashed or is consuming excessive system resources
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The application window is frozen, the computer is unresponsive, or the task manager shows a high percentage of CPU or RAM being used by a single, non-essential process.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Press “Ctrl + Shift + Esc” to open Task Manager, right-click the unresponsive process under the “Processes” tab, and select “End Task” to force termination.

definition: external or internal hardware additions such as secondary hard drives external usb drives or nas network attached storage devices used to expand the storage capacity of a computer
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The system fails to recognize the new drive, or the disk is showing as “Uninitialized” in Disk Management.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check for power and data cable connections, ensure the drive is initialized in the OS, verify the partition style (GPT - GUID Partition Table or MBR - Master Boot Record) matches system needs, and format the drive with a filesystem.

definition: any hardware device capable of storing digital data for long-term use ranging from traditional mechanical hard drives to modern flash-based media
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Frequent file corruption, system failure to boot, clicking sounds coming from the drive, or the OS (Operating System) reporting "Drive not found" errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check all physical power and data connections, use the command “chkdsk /f /r” to scan for and repair sector-level corruption, and replace the drive if SMART (Self-Monitoring, Analysis, and Reporting Technology) diagnostic tools indicate critical failure imminent.

definition: an optical storage medium capable of reading and writing high-density data on blu-ray discs typically used for high-definition video or high-capacity data backups
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The drive fails to spin up, the system does not recognize the inserted disc, or the drive fails to finalize burn processes.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Clean the optical lens with a specialized cleaning disc, check the motherboard SATA (Serial Advanced Technology Attachment) port in the BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) to ensure the device is enabled, and update the optical drive firmware.

definition: a performance restriction where the storage drive's read write speed is significantly slower than the rest of the system components like the cpu or ram causing overall system lag
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The OS takes an excessive amount of time to load, applications take several minutes to launch, and "Disk usage" in Task Manager consistently hits 100%.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Identify the active processes consuming disk I/O (Input/Output), replace a mechanical HDD (Hard Disk Drive) with an SSD (Solid-State Drive), or move the OS to a faster partition.

definition: legacy optical storage drives designed to read write compact discs cd which offer limited capacity approx 700 mb
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The drive makes repetitive grinding noises or cannot read discs that work in other machines.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the power connection to the drive, inspect the IDE (Integrated Drive Electronics) or SATA cable for damage, and ensure the correct optical driver is installed in the Device Manager.

definition: a system tool used to verify the logical integrity of a file system and search for bad sectors on physical storage media
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The OS reports "File system errors" or the drive suddenly becomes read-only.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the command prompt as an administrator and execute the command “chkdsk C: /f /r” to locate and fix logical file system errors and recover readable information from bad sectors.

definition: the physical or logical destruction of storage media to ensure that sensitive data cannot be recovered after the device is decommissioned
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Not applicable (this is an intentional maintenance task).
TROUBLESHOOTING: For SSDs, use the manufacturer's “Secure Erase” utility; for magnetic HDDs, use a degausser or physical destruction methods (shredding, drilling, or crushing the platters).

definition: the regulated process of retiring old hardware by ensuring that storage devices are disposed of according to environmental regulations and data privacy policies
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Not applicable.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Follow organizational documentation regarding data sanitization, physically separate the drive from other e-waste, and use a certified e-waste recycling provider.

definition: an optical storage device that uses laser technology to read and write to digital versatile discs dvd providing a standard capacity of 4 7 gb
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The drive can read some discs but fails to read others, or the drive tray will not open.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check for mechanical obstructions in the tray, update the device drivers, or replace the SATA cable if the system detects the drive but cannot access the media.

definition: a type of non-volatile solid-state storage that can be electronically erased and reprogrammed commonly used in usb drives and sd secure digital cards
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data cannot be written to the device, files become corrupted, or the device is not recognized when plugged into a USB port.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Try a different USB port to rule out motherboard port failure, check for a write-protect switch on the device, or reformat the drive using the “Disk Management” console.

definition: a storage solution that combines a small amount of fast nand negating and logic flash memory for caching with a large-capacity mechanical hdd
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Performance is inconsistent, sometimes fast (when accessing cached data) and sometimes sluggish.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check for drive-specific firmware updates that improve the caching algorithm, and monitor for mechanical failure symptoms consistent with standard HDDs.

word: Storage drives: Magnetic disk drives/HDD (Hard Disk Drive)
definition: traditional storage devices that use spinning magnetic platters and a moving read write head to access and store data
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Clicking or grinding noises, the system takes a long time to access files, or the OS fails to boot due to disk read errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use a SMART monitoring tool to check disk health; if the disk reports reallocated sectors, back up all data immediately and replace the drive.

definition: routine operations such as disk cleanup defragmentation and firmware updates performed to ensure the longevity and performance of storage hardware
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Files take longer to open, system performance gradually degrades, or disk space disappears unexpectedly.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Run the “Disk Cleanup” utility to remove temporary files, use the “Defragment and Optimize Drives” tool to reorganize files (for HDD only, never defrag an SSD), and verify that the OS has enough free space for system operations.

definition: a high-performance interface protocol designed specifically for ssds to communicate directly with the system via the pcie bus drastically reducing latency
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The drive is not recognized by the BIOS/UEFI, or the system crashes during high-speed data transfers.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the motherboard BIOS is updated to support NVMe, check that the drive is fully seated in the M.2 slot, and verify the NVMe driver is installed within the OS.

definition: a category of storage that reads data from or writes data to optical discs cd dvd or blu-ray using laser light
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The device is loud during operation, discs take too long to mount, or the tray is stuck.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Clean the lens, manually eject the tray using the emergency pinhole, and verify that the SATA data/power cable is connected securely.

definition: the logical division of a physical storage drive into separate independent sections that the os sees as individual drives e g c and d
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A drive is full but shows as one large partition, or an OS upgrade fails because the partition structure is invalid.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the “Disk Management” console, right-click the unallocated space, and select “New Simple Volume” to create a new partition, or use a disk utility to resize existing partitions.

word: Storage drives: RAID (Redundant Array of Independent Disks)
definition: a storage technology that uses multiple physical drives to provide redundancy improved performance or both by distributing data across the disks
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The OS reports a "RAID Degraded" status, or a logical volume is missing.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the RAID controller interface at boot, identify the failed drive, replace it, and trigger a "RAID rebuild" operation to re-sync the array.

definition: the physical installation of a new storage drive and the subsequent transfer or restoration of data
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Disk failure or the need for a storage capacity upgrade.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Shut down the system, disconnect the power, remove the old drive, install the new drive, and use cloning software or a backup image to restore the OS and data to the new drive.

definition: the physical interface cables used to connect internal storage drives to the motherboard
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Sporadic disk errors, the drive intermittently drops from the system, or the drive fails to initialize.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Replace the SATA cable with a known-good spare, as these cables are prone to internal wire breaks that are not visible from the outside.

definition: storage drives that use the sata interface for data communication
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Slower transfer speeds or failure to detect in the BIOS.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the SATA cable is securely latched, check the BIOS to ensure the controller mode (AHCI - Advanced Host Controller Interface) is correctly set, and test with a different SATA power cable.

definition: a small non-volatile flash memory card format used primarily for mobile devices cameras and portable computers
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The card is not readable, or it reports "Write protected".
TROUBLESHOOTING: Slide the physical lock switch on the side of the card, attempt to read the card in a different card reader to isolate the fault, and format the card if data is not required.

definition: high-speed storage devices using flash memory that lack moving mechanical parts resulting in significantly faster access times and higher durability than hdds
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System slowdowns, read-only errors, or the system fails to boot.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the drive firmware is updated, check the BIOS for AHCI mode, and use the drive's manufacturer utility to monitor health (TBW - Total Bytes Written).

definition: a systematic approach to diagnosing and resolving storage-related issues
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data loss, system hang, or hardware failure messages.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Follow the "divide and conquer" method: check cables, verify BIOS settings, test the drive in a different system, and use OS-level tools like “chkdsk” or manufacturer utilities.

definition: the configuration that allows a virtual machine to access physical storage or virtual disk files hosted on the host machine
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The virtual machine cannot boot, or it reports that the virtual disk is "Inaccessible".
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the VM configuration file points to the correct path for the virtual disk image, verify the host has enough free space to support the virtual disk, and check file permissions.

definition: the windows interface that provides a visual breakdown of disk space usage by category apps files system storage
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The system reports "Low disk space" warnings.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Navigate to “Settings > System > Storage”, identify which categories (like “Temporary files”) are consuming the most space, and use the built-in “Cleanup recommendations” to free up space.

definition: a windows feature that allows you to group multiple physical disks into a single storage pool which can then be used to create virtual drives with built-in redundancy mirroring or parity
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A drive failure within the pool results in degraded storage performance or warnings in the Settings app.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the “Storage Spaces” management console, identify the failed drive, replace it, and click “Add drive” or “Repair” to integrate the new disk back into the pool.

definition: a type of copper cabling that features a protective foil or mesh shield around the twisted pairs to reduce emi electromagnetic interference
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Network errors persist despite switching to high-quality unshielded cabling, suggesting a high-EMI environment.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Install STP cabling and ensure the shielding is properly grounded to the patch panel or switch to dissipate electrical interference.

definition: a network cable like an ethernet patch cable that has the same pin-out configuration on both ends standard t568b
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Devices are not linking up, or the network shows "No connection".
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the cable type; ensure you are not accidentally using a crossover cable for modern equipment that expects a straight-through pin-out.

definition: a data type composed of letters and numbers often used for passwords product keys or cli command line interface arguments
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Configuration commands fail because the string contains illegal characters.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the string is formatted correctly, check for case-sensitive errors, and confirm no special characters are required or forbidden by the specific application.

definition: a sequence of characters used in programming and command lines to represent text
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Scripts fail to run due to syntax errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check for proper quotation marks (“ ”) around the string and ensure all required delimiters are in place.

definition: a hand tool designed to remove the outer jacket of cables like utp or stp without damaging the internal copper conductors
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Poor network connections caused by nicked or broken internal wires during cable termination.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Adjust the depth of the stripper blade to match the cable jacket thickness, and replace the blade if it is dull and tearing the insulation instead of cutting it.

definition: a condition where a physical key on a keyboard remains depressed or does not register when pressed
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The keyboard types a single character repeatedly, or the system does not respond to key presses.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use compressed air to blow out debris from under the key cap, remove the key cap (if possible) to clean the switch mechanism, or replace the keyboard if the switch itself is faulty.

definition: a pen-shaped input tool used on touchscreen devices for precision control drawing or handwriting
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The stylus does not register input on the screen.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Replace the stylus battery (if active), verify the stylus is paired with the device, and clean the touchscreen surface to remove oils or dust.

definition: a linux unix command substitute user that allows a user to run commands with the privileges of another user usually the superuser root
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Permission denied errors when trying to edit system configuration files.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure you have the correct password for the target user, and use the command “su -” to open a full login shell with root privileges.

definition: a network architecture where a specific sub-network a dmz - demilitarized zone is placed between an internal trusted network and an external untrusted network the internet for added security
ERROR SYMPTOMS: External users cannot reach web services, or internal services are unexpectedly exposed to the internet.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify firewall rules that govern the flow of traffic into and out of the screened subnet to ensure that only intended ports and services are accessible.

definition: a command that allows a permitted user to execute a command as the superuser or another user as specified by the security policy
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Command not found or "User is not in the sudoers file" errors.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the user is added to the “sudo” group, and check the “/etc/sudoers” file for correct configuration using the command “visudo”.

definition: a power device designed to protect electronic equipment from voltage spikes or surges by diverting excess energy to the ground
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Equipment fails to turn on, or the surge protector itself shows a "Fault" or "Not Grounded" indicator.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the wall outlet is properly grounded and replace the surge protector if it has absorbed previous spikes and reached its protection limit.

definition: a sudden short-lived increase in voltage that can damage sensitive electronic components
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System reboots, component failure, or a burnt electrical smell from power supplies.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Connect all sensitive equipment to a high-quality UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) that includes surge suppression and voltage regulation features.

definition: the use of cameras to monitor an area for security or safety purposes often integrated with a network system for remote viewing
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The surveillance feed is blank, laggy, or the recording software shows "Camera disconnected".
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the network switch PoE (Power over Ethernet) status for the camera, verify the IP camera settings, and ensure the DVR (Digital Video Recorder) or NVR (Network Video Recorder) is operational.

definition: an analog video cable standard used to transmit display signals from a computer to a monitor
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The display has a pink or green tint (indicating a broken color pin) or flickering images.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Replace the SVGA cable and ensure all pins are straight before connecting; if the issue persists, the monitor or GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) port may be faulty.

definition: a network device that connects devices on a lan and uses mac media access control addresses to forward data frames only to the intended destination port
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Devices connected to the switch cannot communicate, or the network is experiencing a loop/broadcast storm.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the switch port status lights, reset the switch, or check for port-level configuration errors (e.g., VLAN - Virtual Local Area Network mismatches).

definition: the initial packets sent in a tcp transmission control protocol handshake syn - synchronize to establish a reliable connection between a client and a server
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Connection timed out or "Server unreachable" during service initialization.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use a packet analyzer like “Wireshark” to verify that the SYN packet is leaving the client and that the server is responding with a SYN-ACK (Synchronize-Acknowledgment) packet.

definition: the process of ensuring that data files contacts or settings are identical across multiple devices e g syncing a phone to a cloud account
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Changes made on a desktop are not reflected on a mobile device, or synchronization errors appear in the sync software.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify internet connectivity, check account login status, and clear the sync cache.

definition: the integration of a smartphone with an automobile's onboard computer via bluetooth apple carplay or android auto for hands-free communication and media control
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The phone fails to connect to the vehicle system, or the media controls do not respond.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Forget the device in both the phone's and the car's Bluetooth settings, perform a new pairing process, and ensure the phone's OS is compatible with the vehicle's firmware.

definition: the automated process of keeping data files settings or application states consistent across multiple computing devices often utilizing a central server or cloud-based service to ensure the latest version of data is available everywhere
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Conflicting file versions, missing data on one device, error messages stating "Sync failed", or unexpected high bandwidth and battery usage by background synchronization services.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify internet connectivity, check service status (e.g., OneDrive or iCloud), manually trigger a sync in the application settings, and clear local cache or temporary sync data folders to resolve conflicts.

definition: a service model where data is stored and managed on remote servers the cloud rather than locally allowing for real-time synchronization of files across devices often through platforms like microsoft onedrive google drive or dropbox
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Inability to access shared files from a different device, "Out of storage" notifications, or file synchronization appearing stuck at a certain percentage.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the local sync client settings, ensure the user is signed in with the correct account credentials, check the storage quota on the service provider's web portal, and restart the sync client application.

definition: the synchronization of desktop files application settings and browser preferences across multiple desktop workstations to provide a consistent user experience
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Customized desktop backgrounds or browser bookmarks not transferring to a new computer, or local folder changes not updating on the secondary machine.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Navigate to “Settings > Accounts > Sync your settings” (in Windows), ensure that the "Sync settings" toggle is turned to “On”, and verify that both machines are logged into the same Microsoft or organizational account.

definition: a type of backup created by combining a full base backup with subsequent incremental backups to create a new updated full backup image without requiring a full system read from the original source
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Backup restoration fails with "Corrupted archive" errors, or the backup process takes much longer than scheduled due to data inconsistencies.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Review the backup server logs to identify which incremental files were rejected, perform a manual validation check on the base backup, and run the backup utility in "Verify" mode to ensure integrity.

definition: a centralized server that collects aggregates and stores log messages from various network devices such as routers switches and firewalls to simplify troubleshooting and security auditing
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Log files on individual devices are full, or security teams cannot retrieve historical logs because the centralized server is unreachable.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the network device is correctly configured with the Syslog server's IP address and UDP (User Datagram Protocol) port 514, check for firewall rules blocking log traffic, and verify service availability on the Syslog server host.

definition: a windows system utility used to troubleshoot the boot process by allowing users to manage startup programs boot configuration like safe mode and services
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Windows takes too long to boot, or background services that are not needed are consuming high CPU (Central Processing Unit) resources.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the tool by executing the command “msconfig”, navigate to the “Services” tab (check “Hide all Microsoft services” to avoid disabling critical OS functions), uncheck unnecessary items, and restart the computer.

definition: the diagnostic and repair process for os-level files that have become corrupted deleted or altered by malware or improper shutdowns
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Frequent BSOD (Blue Screen of Death) errors, missing system icons, or applications failing to launch due to missing DLL (Dynamic Link Library) files.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the Command Prompt as an administrator and execute the command “sfc /scannow” to initiate the System File Checker, which scans and automatically replaces damaged system files with valid cached versions.

definition: a recovery feature in the windows re that restores the entire operating system programs and data from a previously created system image file
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The operating system is completely unbootable, or the registry is so damaged that standard repairs fail.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Boot from Windows installation media, select “Repair your computer > Troubleshoot > Advanced Options > System Image Recovery”, and select the external drive or network location containing the saved system image.

definition: a comprehensive windows utility that provides a detailed summary of the computer's hardware system components and software environment
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The user is unsure of the current hardware specifications (RAM, CPU, BIOS version) when trying to install new software or drivers.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Execute the command “msinfo32” in the Run box to view the summary, or use the tool to export a report file for technical support analysis.

definition: recorded events generated by the os or applications that track critical operations errors and warnings for diagnostic purposes
ERROR SYMPTOMS: An application crashes, but the user is unsure why, or a background service fails to start during boot.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the “Event Viewer” by executing the command “eventvwr”, expand “Windows Logs”, and click “System” to review entries marked with “Error” or “Critical” to pinpoint the cause of the failure.

definition: the central control panel in macos now referred to as system settings in newer versions used for configuring hardware networking user accounts and system behavior
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The user cannot change monitor resolution, configure Wi-Fi, or manage login items.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Click the Apple menu, select “System Preferences”, and use the search bar to find the relevant category (e.g., “Displays” or “Network”) to adjust the desired configuration.

definition: a menu within the windows settings app that displays essential information about the computer's os version edition processor ram and computer name
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The computer name is incorrect, or the user needs to verify the license status of Windows.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the Settings app, navigate to “System > About” to view and modify the device name, domain/workgroup settings, or advanced system properties.

definition: the set of minimum hardware cpu speed ram disk space and software os version drivers needed for an application to function correctly
ERROR SYMPTOMS: An application fails to open, crashes during installation, or performs sluggishly even on a functional system.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Compare the manufacturer's provided specification sheet against the system information retrieved via “msinfo32” and upgrade components (like RAM) if they do not meet the minimum requirement.

definition: a feature that reverts the os configuration system files and installed applications to a previous restore point without affecting personal user data
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A recent driver update, Windows update, or software installation has caused the OS to become unstable or crash.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Access Windows RE, select “Troubleshoot > Advanced Options > System Restore”, choose a restore point dated before the issue occurred, and follow the prompts to complete the reversal.

definition: the act of turning off the creation of restore points to save disk space or prevent users from rolling back system configurations
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The option to create or revert to a restore point is missing or greyed out.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Search for “Create a restore point” in the start menu, click “Configure” under the System Protection tab, and select “Disable system protection” to turn it off.

definition: the act of activating the system protection feature to allow the automatic creation of restore points
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Changes to the system cannot be undone, and no restore points exist to revert to.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “System Properties”, go to the “System Protection” tab, select the C: drive, click “Configure”, and select “Turn on system protection” to ensure future changes can be recovered.

definition: the automation of diagnostic or security scans such as virus scans or disk integrity checks to occur at specific intervals
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System performance drops unexpectedly because scans are running during peak usage times.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the “Task Scheduler” by executing the command “taskschd.msc”, locate the task under the Library, and modify the “Triggers” tab to change the schedule to off-peak hours.

definition: the main branch of the windows settings application that houses core system-wide configurations including display notifications power sleep storage and about
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The user cannot change screen brightness, configure multiple monitors, or change power management settings.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Click the Start button, select the “Settings” gear icon, and click “System” to manage the core configuration of the workstation.

definition: a mobile-focused operating system specifically designed for touch-screen tablet devices offering a simplified ui user interface and specialized power management to support long battery life and mobile-specific apps
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Applications frequently crash upon opening, the touch screen does not respond to input, or the device fails to boot past the manufacturer's logo.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Perform a "Force Restart" by holding the power and volume buttons, clear the cache for problematic apps in the settings menu, or perform a "Factory Reset" to revert the OS to its original state.

definition: an open-source linux-based mobile operating system developed by google widely used in various tablet hardware featuring high customizability and the google play store for app distribution
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System UI has stopped errors, excessive battery drain from background services, or difficulty connecting to Wi-Fi (Wireless Fidelity) networks.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Boot into “Recovery Mode” to wipe the system partition cache, uninstall recently installed third-party apps, or check for pending “System Updates” in the settings menu.

definition: the proprietary mobile operating system developed by apple for its ipad and iphone devices characterized by a closed ecosystem and strict app vetting process
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The device becomes stuck in a "Boot Loop" after an update, or apps fail to launch.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Connect the device to a computer and use iTunes or “Finder” to perform an “Update” or “Restore” (which reinstalls the system software).

definition: a derivative of ios specifically tailored for the ipad offering enhanced multitasking features improved file management and stylus support for professional workflows
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Multitasking gestures stop responding, or the “Files” app fails to connect to cloud storage services.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the OS is updated to the latest version, verify that “Multitasking & Gestures” are enabled in Settings, and sign out/back into the Apple ID account.

definition: a security protocol that provides centralized authentication authorization and accounting aaa services for network devices like routers and switches
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Administrators are unable to log into network devices using their enterprise credentials, or accounting records are not appearing on the server.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the server IP address configuration on the network device, ensure the shared secret key matches between the client and the server, and check if UDP port 49 is open.

definition: a physical security breach where an unauthorized person follows an authorized individual into a restricted area without presenting credentials
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Unknown personnel are found in secure server rooms or restricted office spaces.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Implement physical deterrents like mantraps (a two-door security vestibule), install turnstiles, and conduct mandatory employee training on security awareness and physical access protocols.

definition: the process of preparing for and sitting for a professional certification exam such as the comptia a
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Anxiety, time management failure, or failing to address all exam objectives.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use practice simulations, familiarize yourself with the exam structure, and follow a systematic study plan that covers all CompTIA domains.

definition: a strategy used to handle complex high-uncertainty questions during an exam by using process-of-elimination and careful analysis
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Spending too much time on a single question or guessing incorrectly due to panic.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Read the entire prompt carefully, identify keywords, eliminate obviously incorrect answers, flag the question for review, and move to the next item to maintain momentum.

definition: best practices for exam day including preparation focus and adherence to testing center or remote proctoring guidelines
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Arriving late, forgetting required ID, or violating testing center policies.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Schedule the exam in advance, verify ID requirements, get adequate rest, and arrive early to the physical or digital testing environment.

definition: the step of revisiting flagged or skipped questions before finalizing the exam submission
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Submitting an exam with unanswered questions or errors that could have been caught with a second look.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Save time at the end of the exam to systematically review flagged items, ensure no questions were left blank, and verify that your final choice aligns with the prompt's requirements.

definition: a windows utility used for monitoring system performance managing running processes services and startup applications
ERROR SYMPTOMS: System performance is sluggish, the computer is unresponsive, or an application has frozen.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the tool by executing the command “taskmgr” or pressing “Ctrl + Shift + Esc”, navigate to the relevant tab to end unresponsive tasks, or analyze resource utilization.

definition: a tab in task manager that provides a summary of resource usage cpu time and network usage by apps over a specific period
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The user needs to identify which applications are consuming excessive network bandwidth or processor cycles.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Access the “App History” tab, click “Options” in the menu bar, and select “Show history for all processes” to view detailed usage logs for installed applications.

definition: a tab displaying all active applications and background processes running on the system along with their real-time resource usage
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A program has stopped responding or is consuming 100% of the CPU or memory.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Locate the problematic process in the list, right-click it, and select “End task” to terminate it forcefully.

definition: a tab that lists all windows services background programs that run independently of user interaction and their current status running or stopped
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A critical system feature (like Print Spooler) is not working because its underlying service failed to start.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Go to the “Services” tab, right-click a service, and select “Start”, “Stop”, or “Restart” to resolve service-level faults.

definition: a tab that manages the programs that automatically launch when the user logs into the windows os
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The system takes an excessive amount of time to reach the desktop, or unnecessary background tools are consuming memory.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Select the “Startup” tab, identify unwanted applications, right-click them, and select “Disable” to prevent them from launching at boot.

definition: a tab that shows all users currently logged into the computer and the processes associated with each user session
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A user needs to log off another user account that is locked or consuming system resources in the background.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Expand the user's name in the “Users” tab, right-click the specific application or process, or right-click the user to “Disconnect” or “Sign off” their session.

definition: a windows administrative tool used to automate tasks running programs scripts or maintenance at specific times or in response to triggers
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Automated backups, disk cleanup, or security scans are failing to execute at their designated times.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the tool by executing the command “taskschd.msc”, check the task's “History” tab for error codes, and verify the “Triggers” and “Actions” configuration settings.

definition: the long horizontal or vertical bar usually located at the bottom of the windows desktop that provides access to the start menu pinned apps and system tray
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The taskbar is frozen, icons are missing, or it is hidden when it should be visible.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Restart the “Windows Explorer” process via Task Manager, right-click the taskbar to check “Taskbar settings”, or unlock the taskbar to reposition it.

definition: a connection-oriented transport layer protocol that ensures reliable ordered and error-checked delivery of data between applications over an ip internet protocol network
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data packets are lost, files are corrupted during transfer, or connections time out because the handshake cannot complete.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use network diagnostic tools like “ping” or “netstat” to check connectivity, and examine firewall logs to ensure that the required TCP ports are not being blocked.

definition: a mechanism within tcp that prevents a sender from overwhelming a receiver with more data than it can process at one time
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Network performance is significantly lower than the theoretical throughput, suggesting that the flow control mechanism is limiting transmission speeds.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Monitor the network traffic with a packet analyzer to check for “TCP ZeroWindow” messages, which indicate that the receiver's buffer is full.

definition: a combination of an ip address and a port number e g 192 168 1 1 80 that identifies a specific endpoint for a network communication
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Applications cannot connect to a service, or a "Port already in use" error appears.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Execute the command “netstat -an” to view all active socket connections and verify which process is holding a specific port.

definition: the method used by tcp to establish a connection between a client and server consisting of three steps syn syn-ack and ack
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A client fails to establish a connection to a server (e.g., website times out).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use a packet capture tool like “Wireshark” to see if the SYN packet is being sent, and determine if the server is responding with a SYN-ACK or if the packet is dropped by a firewall.

definition: the maximum amount of heat in watts that a computer component usually a cpu or gpu is expected to generate under normal workload used to determine cooling requirements
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The computer shuts down unexpectedly during heavy tasks, or the cooling fan runs at maximum speed constantly.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Ensure the heatsink and fan are sufficient for the component's TDP, replace thermal paste, and clean dust from the intake vents.

definition: the process of turning off the automatic collection and transmission of usage performance and diagnostic data from the os to the software vendor like microsoft
ERROR SYMPTOMS: User privacy concerns or a desire to reduce background network bandwidth usage.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the “Services” console, find and stop the “Connected User Experiences and Telemetry” service, and set its “Startup type” to “Disabled”.

definition: an insecure legacy network protocol used for remote login and management of network devices
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Network traffic is intercepted, or credentials are stolen due to a lack of encryption.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Disable Telnet on all devices and replace it with a secure alternative like SSH (Secure Shell), which provides encryption and secure authentication.

definition: environmental settings managed in data centers to prevent overheating component damage or electrostatic discharge esd
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Hardware fails prematurely, or systems crash due to thermal overload.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Install sensors to monitor server room climate, use HVAC (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning) systems to maintain ideal temperatures (usually between 68°F and 72°F) and humidity levels (between 40% and 60%).

definition: the command-line interface in macos that allows users to interact with the underlying unix-based system using text commands
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A user cannot change system permissions or perform network diagnostics via the GUI (Graphical User Interface).
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “Terminal” from the “Utilities” folder, and use commands like “sudo” or “ping” to perform administrative tasks or network troubleshooting.

definition: a powershell command used to test whether a remote computer is reachable over a network acting similarly to the ping command but with more robust output
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A user cannot verify if a remote server is online or responsive.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open “PowerShell” and execute the command “test-connection -computername [IP Address]” to verify the network path and response time.

definition: a handheld tool used to verify the continuity and proper wiring of network cables like utp - unshielded twisted-pair
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Network cables are physically intact but are failing to transmit data.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Connect both ends of the cable to the cable tester, verify the sequence of the lights (1–8) to ensure all pairs are mapped correctly and not crossed.

definition: the process of using a cable tester to ensure that patch cables are correctly wired and functional before installing them in a production network
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Intermittent connectivity issues on a specific workstation.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Test the patch cable being used by the workstation; if it fails, replace it with a new, tested cable.

definition: the regular verification process of ensuring that backup data is not corrupted and can be restored successfully
ERROR SYMPTOMS: An actual disaster occurs and the organization finds the backup files are unreadable or incomplete.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Schedule monthly "restoration tests" where a random subset of data is restored from the backup server to a test environment to confirm file integrity.

definition: the process of verifying that the bios uefi unified extensible firmware interface is functioning correctly and is up to date
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Hardware (like a new CPU) is not detected correctly, or the system crashes during the boot process.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the manufacturer's website for firmware updates, and use the BIOS update utility to flash the firmware to the latest version.

definition: the practice of stressing the cpu to verify its stability speed and thermal performance
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Spontaneous reboots during high-load tasks.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Run a stress-test tool (e.g., Prime95) to monitor the CPU temperature and voltage; if errors occur, the CPU may be overheating or unstable due to overclocking.

definition: the process of checking the physical ram modules for defects or errors
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Random system crashes, "Blue Screen of Death" errors, or file corruption.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Execute the command “mdsched.exe” (Windows Memory Diagnostic tool) or use MemTest86 to scan the RAM for hardware errors.

definition: a series of diagnostic tests performed by the bios uefi on hardware components cpu ram video immediately after the computer is powered on
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The computer makes beeping noises or displays an error code on the screen before the OS loads.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Consult the motherboard manual to decode the POST beep codes, which indicate which hardware component is failing the initialization test.

definition: the process of printing a test page to verify that a printer is correctly configured has sufficient ink toner and is communicating with the print server
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Documents are not printing, or the printer displays an error.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use the printer's on-device menu to print a “Test Page” or “Configuration Page”; if that fails, check the printer's network connectivity or paper tray.

definition: verifying that the psu is delivering stable correct voltages to all internal components
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The computer won't turn on, or random hardware failures occur.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use a multimeter to check the voltage on the ATX (Advanced Technology eXtended) pins to see if they are within the acceptable tolerance (+/- 5%).

definition: the act of verifying ram integrity by either using software tests or the physical swap-and-test method
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Frequent application crashes or BSODs.
TROUBLESHOOTING: If software tests (like Windows Memory Diagnostic) fail, physically remove one RAM stick at a time to isolate which specific module is faulty.

definition: the practice of running new or untrusted software in a secure isolated environment a sandbox to ensure it does not compromise the host system
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Malware or poorly written scripts are affecting the host OS.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Use virtual machine software or a built-in “Windows Sandbox” to run the application, monitor the host's behavior, and delete the sandbox environment once the test is complete.

word: Testing: Theories of probable cause, CompTIA troubleshooting process
definition: a core step in the comptia troubleshooting methodology where the technician hypothesizes potential causes based on gathered information
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Indiscriminate "shotgun" troubleshooting that wastes time and does not solve the issue.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Review the symptoms, consider the most likely causes first (Occam's Razor), document each theory, and prioritize them from simplest to most complex.

definition: stressing the graphics hardware to verify stability under high-graphical workloads
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Artifacts on the screen (glitches), games crashing, or system freezing.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Run a GPU stress test (like FurMark) and monitor temperatures; ensure the GPU driver is updated, and check that the PCIe (Peripheral Component Interconnect Express) power cables are firmly connected.

definition: validating the configuration and performance of a virtual machine before deploying it into a production environment
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The VM is slow, cannot connect to the network, or fails to boot.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Check the VM's virtual resource allocation (CPU/RAM), verify the virtual network switch settings, and ensure the hypervisor is running the latest updates.

definition: the process of sharing a mobile device's cellular data connection with a workstation or laptop using a physical usb universal serial bus cable allowing the host computer to access the internet through the mobile device's network
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The host computer displays a "No Internet Access" icon when connected to the phone, or the mobile device does not surface the option to enable network sharing over a cable interface.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Connect the mobile device via a verified data-sync USB (Universal Serial Bus) cable, navigate to “Settings > Network & Internet > Hotspot & tethering” on the device, toggle the “USB tethering” switch to “On”, and open the host computer's Device Manager to confirm the mobile broadband network adapter driver is initialized.

definition: physical security events involving the unauthorized removal or misplacement of corporate mobile assets requiring logical mitigations to prevent unauthorized data exfiltration or access to enterprise infrastructure
ERROR SYMPTOMS: An corporate asset is flagged as missing by an employee, or MDM (Mobile Device Management) access logs show unauthorized login attempts or anomalies indicating a physical device compromise.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Log into the enterprise MDM (Mobile Device Management) control panel utility, track the coordinates of the device via GPS (Global Positioning System), send a remote lock instruction command, and execute a remote wipe script to sanitize all internal flash storage partitions if recovery is impossible.

word: Theories of probable cause, CompTIA troubleshooting process
definition: the second step of the systematic 6-step comptia computing technology industry association core troubleshooting methodology wherein a technician analyzes gathered data to brainstorm potential failure origins prioritizing the simplest possibilities first
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Technicians executing aimless, uncoordinated hardware component replacements, resulting in extended operational downtime and high ticket remediation expenses due to a lack of root-cause logic.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Question the user regarding system modifications, analyze system logs, isolate the failing subsystem, apply logical deduction starting with the easiest variables (such as checking loose power plugs), and document the prioritized list of potential causes before proceeding to actual testing phase verification blocks.

definition: a type of consumer and office printing hardware that utilizes tiny electrical resistors to flash-heat liquid ink within the print head forming a high-pressure vapor bubble that forces a droplet out of the nozzle orifice onto the page
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Printed text exhibits missing lines, faded color bands, or completely blank areas despite new fluid cartridges being installed into the carriage framework assembly.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the printing utility layout preference menu, select the “Clean Printhead” instruction task macro, print an alignment sheet pattern layout, or remove the target cartridge block entirely and gently wipe the lower nozzle surface using a lint-free electronic cleaning swab to clear dry, coagulated residue.

definition: a highly conductive compound applied directly between a processor's integrated heat spreader and a cooling block assembly to fill microscopic surface air gaps and facilitate optimal heat transfer
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The system encounters spontaneous reboots or freezes under mild operational stress, or motherboard monitors report CPU (Central Processing Unit) internal temperatures spiking rapidly above safe limits.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Power down the computer, detach the cooling fan structure from the motherboard anchors, clean old, dry paste off the surfaces using a cloth dipped in pure isopropyl alcohol, place a small dot of clean thermal paste onto the center of the CPU (Central Processing Unit) surface, and firmly clamp down the heat sink uniformly.

definition: a reliable quiet printing technology that produces an image by delivering selective localized heat arrays from a thermal print head onto special chemically treated heat-sensitive media
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Paper passes through the output slot completely blank, printed barcodes appear blurred and unreadable by scanning sensors, or the internal roller engine generates loud slipping noise patterns.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Verify the paper roll orientation is not inverted (only one side of thermal paper reacts to heat), clean the print head with a specialized cleaning pen containing isopropyl alcohol, and check the spring tension arm mechanisms.

definition: the collective electromechanical sub-assemblies inside a thermal printing device specifically the thermal print head heating nodes the rubber platen roller media advancement paper feed sensors and tension spring mechanisms
ERROR SYMPTOMS: The printing output displays narrow, permanent white streaks running vertically down the receipt page length, suggesting individual heating array element burnt states.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the internal printer compartment assembly structure panel, inspect the rubber platen roller element for flat spots or deep pitting distortions, use compressed air to blow paper dust off the tracking sensor eyes, and substitute the print head array block if tracking elements are defective.

definition: the routine cleaning and operational tuning of a thermal printer to maximize service lifespan involving residue removal from the print head and platen roller as well as checking the paper cutting blade
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Receipt records twist sideways inside the feed track channel causing paper jams, or dark black smudges build up continuously across the face of output media sheets.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Open the main service latch door of the printer assembly, pull loose the spent media wheel casing core, use a specialized electronic cleaning pad saturated with 99% isopropyl alcohol to wipe residue off the print head, spin and clean the rubber platen roller surface area, and carefully trim any structural adhesive debris off the cutter teeth blocks.

definition: the exact non-impact digital reproduction cycle where electrical impulses selectively activate high-density miniature heating nodes on a print head as heat-sensitive paper moves past triggering a chemical color change without any ribbon ink components
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Images show uneven contrast distributions or distorted aspect ratios because the electronic timing coordination sync parameters between heat intervals and platen advancement cycles are failing.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Access the device advanced firmware manager screen page options tab, reset density settings, print an internal diagnostic configuration report loop, and verify input power values conform exactly to the manufacturer specification rules.

definition: a threat is any potential event or adversary looking to exploit an information system whereas a vulnerability represents an unpatched software code error logical flaw or physical design weakness that allows a threat to succeed
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Threat intelligence monitoring software alerts administrators of unpatched system processes, or networks experience unauthorized infiltration vectors targeting default configurations.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Execute a comprehensive vulnerability assessment scan across all subnets using specialized network security auditing tools, isolate exposed endpoints immediately, prioritize critical code anomalies, and apply official vendor software patch installations to seal the flaws.

definition: the implementation of a layered defense-in-depth framework consisting of strict access management system updates regular security training and network segmentation to manage environmental risk exposure profiles
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Systems suffer from configuration drift, outdated endpoint security configurations, or repeated internal policy exceptions that leave network assets highly exposed to compromise.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Mandate multi-factor authentication (MFA) across all user directory models, establish automated patch distribution policies via central update utilities, block dangerous ports (such as port 23 or 21) at the network perimeter firewall, and conduct routine technical penetration testing loops.

definition: an aggressive online or offline security exploitation technique where an adversary utilizes automated software to systematically attempt every possible character string combination to crack a user password or encryption token signature block
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Security event dashboards flag an abnormal volume of failed account authentication attempts referencing sequential patterns, high CPU (Central Processing Unit) load on directory servers, and multiple simultaneous user lockouts.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Access the Windows “Local Security Policy” utility framework panel by executing the instruction command “secpol.msc”, navigate directly to “Account Policies > Account Lockout Policy”, adjust the setting parameter for “Account lockout threshold” to 5 attempts, and enforce complex character length boundaries.

definition: the scientific evaluation and logical cracking of cryptographic systems to bypass structural data encryption mechanisms and uncover plaintext contents without holding the authorized decryption keys
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Data transmissions across wireless or wide-area loops are intercepted and decrypted by un-authorized entities due to the active deployment of obsolete or broken algorithms.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Decommission weak legacy security algorithms (such as WEP - Wired Equivalent Privacy or DES - Data Encryption Standard), enforce strong asymmetric and symmetric standards like AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) containing 256-bit key parameters, and change operational shared cryptographic keys frequently.

definition: a publicly accessible standardized dictionary catalog database that assigns tracking nomenclature numbers e g cve-2026-xxxx to documented security vulnerabilities in software and hardware products helping technicians manage patch coordination workflows
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Security auditors inform the IT (Information Technology) team that local enterprise server versions contain unmitigated, critically rated software vulnerabilities, but administrators lack technical details to address them.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Search the specific reference string index inside your central corporate vulnerability analyzer interface or via public database repositories, identify the exact affected software version dependencies, download the matching manufacturer firmware patch element, and run the mitigation upgrade process inside a sandbox environment first.

definition: a large-scale network security attack where an adversary synchronizes thousands of geographically decentralized internet-connected computing nodes zombies or a botnet to flood a target web service with data traffic overwhelming its capacity and causing a crash
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Upstream external edge routers drop synchronization frames, internet portal pages time out with gateway errors, and network performance logs highlight near-100% bandwidth load originating from disparate global IP (Internet Protocol) pools.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Engage with an upstream cloud-based traffic-scrubbing provider to divert incoming data streams, configure edge firewall network access control lists to filter out malicious traffic signatures, rate-limit ingress connection queues at the peripheral boundary, and sinkhole target routes if necessary to protect underlying network nodes.

definition: a variant password-cracking attack methodology where specialized password-guessing tools load a precompiled plaintext text document file containing thousands of standard words phrases and common variations to systematically find an account credential match
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Audit scripts uncover standard words utilized as network access passwords, or account security monitoring daemons record rapid, alphabetized credential validation failure sequences across server nodes.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Enforce complex password composition rules through Active Directory Group Policy Objects (GPOs), integrate automated checks that block users from picking strings present in public dictionary word files, and supplement local network entry loops with multi-factor authentication (MFA).

definition: an attack originating from a singular source system designed to disrupt or disable a target network computer server's operational services by consuming its local resource bounds such as cpu cycles memory frames or storage queues
ERROR SYMPTOMS: A specific production line server or network switch becomes completely unresponsive to requests, but network traffic capture loops show the input strain is traceable back to one isolated source IP (Internet Protocol) address configuration.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Identify the attacking network interface trace layout using tools like Wireshark, launch the peripheral network firewall management panel console layer, inject an immediate inbound block rule targeting that specific source address node, and power-cycle internal state connections to drop hanging session queues.

definition: a class of software security vulnerabilities where untrusted or unvalidated user input is passed directly to an internal interpreter engine as part of a runtime command instruction tricking the core software application into executing unauthorized code blocks
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Application error logs dump underlying system database structure outputs directly onto public interface screens, user security privileges undergo unauthorized elevation, or background application configurations change without consent.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Enforce strict input data character parameters and server-side white-list code checks across all input entry forms, adopt parameterized queries and prepared statements during software creation cycles, and deploy a specialized WAF (Web Application Firewall) to filter ingress web application traffic streams.

definition: security risk liabilities originating from individuals who hold authorized credential access parameters inside an organization's network perimeter boundary such as current employees rogue contractors or former staff who abuse their privileges to compromise data assets or disrupt architecture states
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Proprietary database entries undergo un-authorized structural replication or export sequences during odd, non-business hours, file permission boundaries are bypassed locally, or network configurations undergo hostile manipulation from internal workstation terminals.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Enforce the technical framework Principal of Least Privilege (PoLP), disable inheritance parameters across secure directory trees, implement continuous activity log monitoring via a SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) platform tool, and execute immediate account suspension routines during employee offboarding cycles.

definition: the multi-faceted technical practice of recovering plaintext user credentials from intercepted network data captures or from compromised database password cryptographic hash strings using high-performance specialized cracking software tools
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Corporate network auditing utilities detect simple or easily decryptable security strings assigned to administrative user profiles, or network sniffers isolate unencrypted password packets moving over open internal protocols.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Standardize the implementation of secure, salted, slow-hashing data functions (such as Argon2 or bcrypt) for local system identity databases, restrict the use of plaintext network services (like port 21 or 23), and replace traditional basic login requirements with certificate-based smart card or biometric multi-factor authentication (MFA) parameters.

definition: a deceptive network security exploitation vector where a malicious actor falsifies protocol tracking attributes such as constructing fake source ip addresses forging email sender addresses or spoofing hardware mac addresses to impersonate a trusted entity
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Network switches become confused by competing hardware address metrics, or employees act upon malicious instructions contained within phishing emails that visually mimic local executive accounts.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Enable security mechanisms such as MAC (Media Access Control) address binding and port security on local hardware switches, configure robust protocol verification records including SPF (Sender Policy Framework), DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail), and DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance) inside public DNS (Domain Name System) record files, and activate reverse-path forwarding checks on internal routers.

definition: a specific attack variant targeting backend database servers where an adversary inputs malformed database command strings into web application form boxes forcing the engine to return sensitive data files or drop internal tables
ERROR SYMPTOMS: Web application login screens allow access when a dummy statement string (such as “' OR '1'='1”) is entered, database tracking indexes disappear, or internal log entries record erratic script failures within SQL processing modules.
TROUBLESHOOTING: Sanitize all application inputs to strip dangerous punctuation elements, replace dynamic string concatenation habits with rigid input parameters and prepared statement templates, and ensure the database management system account privileges conform strictly to a non-administrative execution scope.
